title.raw: 卷110 食貨志六 Volume 110 Treatise 6: Finance and Economics

sentences.zh: 夫為國為家者，莫不以穀貨為本。

translations.literal: Those who govern a state or a family—none fail to take grain and goods as their foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever rules a state or runs a household invariably treats grain and currency as the foundation of all else.

sentences.zh: 故洪範八政，以食為首，其在易曰「聚人曰財」，周禮以九職任萬民，以九賦斂財賄。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Hong Fan's eight administrative concerns food comes first; in the Changes it says, 'To assemble people is called wealth'; the Rites of Zhou assign the nine occupations to the myriad people and collect wealth with the nine levies.
translations.idiomatic: In the Great Plan's eight domains of government, food ranks first; the Book of Changes says that gathering people is called wealth; and the Rites of Zhou charge the myriad people with nine occupations while levying wealth through nine taxes.

sentences.zh: 是以古先哲王莫不敬授民時，務農重穀，躬親千畝，貢賦九州。

translations.literal: Therefore the wise kings of antiquity all respectfully granted the seasons to the people, made agriculture their task and grain their priority, personally plowed the thousand-acre field, and received tribute and levies from the nine provinces.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the sage kings of old all reverently set the seasons for the people, put farming first and valued grain, plowed the ceremonial field themselves, and received tribute and taxes from the nine regions.

sentences.zh: 且一夫不耕，一女不織，或受其飢寒者。

translations.literal: Moreover, if one man does not plow or one woman does not weave, someone will suffer hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: When even one man leaves the field untilled or one woman the loom idle, someone will go hungry or cold.

sentences.zh: 飢寒迫身，不能保其赤子，攘竊而犯法，以至於殺身。

translations.literal: When hunger and cold press upon the body, one cannot protect one's infant children; one grabs and steals and violates the law, even to the point of losing one's life.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by hunger and cold, people cannot protect their own children; they steal and break the law, even unto death.

sentences.zh: 迹其所由，王政所陷也。

translations.literal: Tracing whence this comes, it is where royal government has fallen short.
translations.idiomatic: Trace the cause back, and you find failures of royal government at the root.

sentences.zh: 夫百畝之內，勿奪其時，易其田疇，薄其稅斂，民可使富也。

translations.literal: Within the hundred-mu allotments, do not seize their seasons, improve their fields, lighten their taxes and levies—the people can be made wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: Within each hundred-mu plot, if you do not steal their seasons, reform their fields, and lighten taxes and levies, the people can be made prosperous.

sentences.zh: 既飽且富，而仁義禮節生焉，亦所謂衣食足，識榮辱也。

translations.literal: Once sated and wealthy, then benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and propriety arise—this too is what is called 'when clothing and food are sufficient, one knows honor and shame.'
translations.idiomatic: Once people are fed and prosperous, benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and decorum take root—as the saying goes, only when clothing and food are ample do people discern honor from shame.

sentences.zh: 晉末，天下大亂，生民道盡，或死於干戈，或斃於飢饉，其幸而自存者蓋十五焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin the realm fell into great disorder; the path of the living was exhausted—some died in arms, some perished in famine; of those fortunate enough to survive themselves, perhaps one in fifteen remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Jin, the empire collapsed into chaos. The common people were all but extinguished—some fell to war, others to famine. Of those who by luck survived, scarcely one in fifteen remained.

sentences.zh: 太祖定中原，接喪亂之弊，兵革並起，民廢農業。

translations.literal: The Taizu pacified the Central Plain, inheriting the ravages of devastation and disorder; war arose on every side and the people abandoned agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu pacified the Central Plain, he took over a land ruined by devastation. War flared everywhere, and the people abandoned farming.

sentences.zh: 方事雖殷，然經略之先，以食為本，使東平公儀墾闢河北，自五原至于棝陽塞外為屯田。

translations.literal: Though affairs were pressing, in planning strategy food came first; he had the Eastern Peace Duke Yi open and reclaim Hebei, establishing garrison farms from Wuyuan to beyond the Yuyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Though military affairs were urgent, he put food first in grand strategy, sending the Eastern Peace Duke Yi to open Hebei for settlement and establish garrison farms from Wuyuan to beyond the Yuyang frontier pass.

sentences.zh: 初，登國六年破衞辰，收其珍寶、畜產，名馬三十餘萬、牛羊四百餘萬，漸增國用。

translations.literal: At first, in the sixth year of Dengguo he defeated Wei Chen, seizing his treasures and livestock—more than three hundred thousand fine horses and over four million cattle and sheep—gradually increasing state revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, in the sixth year of Dengguo, he defeated Wei Chen and seized his treasures and herds—over three hundred thousand fine horses and more than four million head of cattle and sheep—steadily swelling the state's resources.

sentences.zh: 既定中山，分徙吏民及徒何種人、工伎巧十萬餘家以充京都，各給耕牛，計口授田。

translations.literal: Once Zhongshan was pacified, he relocated officials, commoners, Tuohe tribespeople, and skilled artisans—more than one hundred thousand households—to fill the capital region, giving each plow oxen and allotting fields by head count.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongshan was secured, he resettled officials, commoners, Tuohe tribespeople, and skilled craftsmen—more than one hundred thousand households—to populate the capital region, issuing plow oxen to each and distributing land according to household size.

sentences.zh: 天興初，制定京邑，東至代郡，西及善無，南極陰館，北盡參合，為畿內之田；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing he fixed the capital domain: east to Dai Commandery, west to Shanyu, south to the limit of Yinyang, north to Canhe—all as fields within the metropolitan belt.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianxing era he defined the capital domain: east to Dai Commandery, west to Shanyu, south to Yinyang, north to Canhe—all as farmland within the metropolitan circuit.

sentences.zh: 其外四方四維置八部帥以監之，勸課農耕，量校收入，以為殿最。

translations.literal: Beyond that, in the four directions and four corners he placed eight division commanders to oversee them, urging agricultural labor, measuring and verifying yields, and using these for performance rankings.
translations.idiomatic: Outside this belt he stationed eight division commanders in the four quarters to supervise farming, urge cultivation, and audit harvests, using the results to rank officials as foremost or last.

sentences.zh: 又躬耕籍田率先百姓。

translations.literal: He also personally plowed the ceremonial field, taking the lead before the common people.
translations.idiomatic: He also plowed the ceremonial field himself, setting an example for the people.

sentences.zh: 自後比歲大熟，匹中八十餘斛。

translations.literal: Thereafter year after year brought great harvests; each bolt-field yielded more than eighty hu.
translations.idiomatic: In the years that followed harvests were abundant year after year, with more than eighty hu per allotted field.

sentences.zh: 是時戎車不息，雖頻有年，猶未足以久贍矣。

translations.literal: At that time war chariots never ceased; though good years came often, it was still not enough for long-term sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: War never ceased in those years; though harvests were frequent, the grain was still not enough to sustain the realm for long.

sentences.zh: 太宗永興中，頻有水旱，詔簡宮人非所當御及非執作伎巧，自餘出賜鰥民。

translations.literal: In the Yongxing era of Taizong floods and droughts came repeatedly; an edict selected out palace women not for the imperial bed or for skilled crafts, and the rest were released and given in marriage to widowers.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizong's Yongxing era repeated floods and droughts struck. An edict screened out palace women not reserved for the emperor or skilled in crafts, and the rest were released to marry widowers among the people.

sentences.zh: 神瑞二年，又不熟，京畿之內，路有行饉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenrui the harvest failed again; within the capital region, travelers on the roads carried provisions with them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenrui crops failed again. Throughout the capital region people took food with them even on short journeys.

sentences.zh: 帝以飢將遷都於鄴，用博士崔浩計乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of famine, was about to move the capital to Ye; on the advice of the academician Cui Hao he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Famine nearly drove the emperor to move the capital to Ye, but he abandoned the plan on the advice of the academician Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 於是分簡尤貧者就食山東。

translations.literal: Thereupon he selected out the poorest to go east of the mountains for food.
translations.idiomatic: He then singled out the poorest families and sent them east of the mountains to find food.

sentences.zh: 敕有司勸課留農者曰：「前志有之，人生在勤，勤則不匱。

translations.literal: He charged the officials to urge agricultural labor and retain farmers, saying: 'Former records have it: human life lies in diligence; with diligence there is no want.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the authorities to urge farming and keep peasants on the land, saying: 'The old records teach that life depends on diligence; the diligent never go wanting.

sentences.zh: 凡庶民之不畜者祭無牲，不耕者祭無盛，不樹者死無槨，不蠶者衣無帛，不績者喪無衰。

translations.literal: Among the common people, those who do not raise livestock have no victims for sacrifice; those who do not plow have no full offerings; those who do not plant trees have no coffin at death; those who do not raise silkworms have no silk for clothing; those who do not spin have no mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners who keep no livestock may offer no sacrificial animals; those who do not farm may present no full offerings; those who plant no trees go without coffins at death; those who raise no silkworms wear no silk; those who do not spin hemp have no mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 教行三農，生殖九穀；

translations.literal: Teach and practice the three fields of agriculture, producing and nurturing the nine grains;
translations.idiomatic: Teach the three fields of agriculture and grow the nine grains;

sentences.zh: 教行園囿，毓長草木；

translations.literal: teach and practice gardens and parks, nurturing trees and plants;
translations.idiomatic: teach orchard and park cultivation and foster trees and plants;

sentences.zh: 教行虞衡，山澤作材；

translations.literal: teach and practice forest and marsh oversight, making mountains and marshes yield materials;
translations.idiomatic: teach forestry and marsh management to draw timber from hills and wetlands;

sentences.zh: 教行藪牧，養蕃鳥獸；

translations.literal: teach and practice meadow pasturage, raising and multiplying birds and beasts;
translations.idiomatic: teach meadow and pasture keeping to breed birds and beasts in abundance;

sentences.zh: 教行百工，飭成器用；

translations.literal: teach and practice the hundred crafts, completing tools and utensils;
translations.idiomatic: teach the hundred crafts to finish tools and wares;

sentences.zh: 教行商賈，阜通貨賄；

translations.literal: teach and practice merchants and traders, enriching the circulation of goods and wealth;
translations.idiomatic: teach trade and commerce to enrich the flow of goods and wealth;

sentences.zh: 教行嬪婦，化治絲枲；

translations.literal: teach and practice palace women, transforming and managing silk and hemp;
translations.idiomatic: teach palace women to work silk and hemp;

sentences.zh: 教行臣妾，事勤力役。

translations.literal: teach and practice servants and concubines, diligently performing labor and corvée.'
translations.idiomatic: teach servants and concubines to labor diligently at their tasks.'

sentences.zh: 」自是民皆力勤，故歲數豐穰，畜牧滋息。

translations.literal: From then on the people all exerted themselves in diligence; therefore for several years harvests were abundant and livestock multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the people worked with all their strength, and for years harvests were plentiful while herds and flocks multiplied.

sentences.zh: 泰常六年，詔六部民羊滿百口，調戎馬一匹。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taichang an edict required that among the six-division people, for every hundred sheep one war horse was levied.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taichang an edict levied one war horse for every hundred sheep among the people of the six divisions.

sentences.zh: 先是，禁網疏闊，民多逃隱。

translations.literal: Before this, prohibitions and regulations were lax and broad, and many among the people fled and concealed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the regulatory net was loose, and many people evaded registration.

sentences.zh: 天興中，詔採諸漏戶，令輸綸綿。

translations.literal: In the Tianxing era an edict gathered all omitted households and required them to pay silk floss.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxing era an edict rounded up unregistered households and required them to pay silk floss in tax.

sentences.zh: 自後諸逃戶占為細繭羅縠者甚眾。

translations.literal: Afterward many fugitive households registered as producers of fine cocoons, gauze, and patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward a great many fugitive households registered as producers of fine silk, gauze, and patterned fabrics.

sentences.zh: [1]於是雜營戶帥遍於天下，不隸守宰，賦役不周，戶口錯亂。

translations.literal: Thereupon miscellaneous camp household chiefs spread throughout the realm; they were not subordinate to prefects and magistrates, levies and corvée were incomplete, and household registers fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous camp household chiefs then spread across the empire. They answered to no prefect or magistrate, taxes and corvée went uncollected, and household registers fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 始光三年詔一切罷之，以屬郡縣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shiguang an edict abolished them all and placed them under commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shiguang an edict abolished them entirely and placed the households under commandery and county administration.

sentences.zh: 神䴥二年，帝親御六軍，略地廣漠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenjue the emperor personally led the six armies to seize territory across the vast desert.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenjue the emperor personally led the six armies on campaign across the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 分命諸將，窮追蠕蠕，東至澣海，西接張掖，北度燕然山，大破之，虜其種落及馬牛雜畜方物萬計。

translations.literal: He dispatched the generals in separate commands to pursue the Rouran to the end; east to the Han Sea, west connecting with Zhangye, north crossing Mount Yanran—they inflicted a great defeat, capturing their tribes and clans together with horses, cattle, miscellaneous livestock, and regional products numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his generals in separate columns to run the Rouran to ground—east to the Han Sea, west to Zhangye, north across Mount Yanran—routing them utterly and capturing their tribes together with horses, cattle, herds, and regional goods beyond count.

sentences.zh: 其後復遣成周公萬度歸西伐焉耆，其王鳩尸卑那單騎奔龜茲，舉國臣民負錢懷貨，一時降款，獲其奇寶異玩以巨萬，駝馬雜畜不可勝數。

translations.literal: Later he again sent the Duke of Cheng, Wandu Gui, to attack Yanqi in the west; its king Jushibina fled alone on horseback to Kucha; the entire state's officials and people, bearing money and clutching goods, submitted at once; they obtained rare treasures and exotic curios numbering in the tens of thousands, and camels, horses, and miscellaneous livestock beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sent the Duke of Cheng, Wandu Gui, west against Yanqi. Its king Jushibina fled alone to Kucha while the whole kingdom, laden with money and goods, surrendered at once. The army seized rare treasures by the myriad and camels, horses, and livestock beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 度歸遂入龜茲，復獲其殊方瓌詭之物億萬已上。

translations.literal: Wandu Gui then entered Kucha and again obtained exotic and marvelous goods from distant regions numbering more than a hundred million.
translations.idiomatic: Wandu Gui then entered Kucha and seized yet more exotic marvels from distant lands—goods worth well over a hundred million.

sentences.zh: 是時方隅未克，帝屢親戎駕，而委政於恭宗。

translations.literal: At that time the border regions were not yet subdued; the emperor repeatedly took the field in person while entrusting government to the Gongzong [Crown Prince].
translations.idiomatic: The frontier was not yet pacified. The emperor campaigned in person again and again while entrusting civil affairs to the Gongzong.

sentences.zh: 真君中，恭宗下令修農職之教，事在帝紀。

translations.literal: In the Zhenjun era the Gongzong issued orders to restore the teachings of agricultural duties; the matter is recorded in the imperial annals.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenjun era the Gongzong ordered the restoration of agricultural instruction; the details appear in the imperial annals.

sentences.zh: 此後數年之中，軍國用足矣。

translations.literal: In the several years thereafter, military and state expenditures were sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the army and the state were fully supplied.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，牧守之官，頗為貨利。

translations.literal: In the time of Gaozong, pastoral and defending officials were quite given to profit through goods.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong many provincial governors pursued illicit profit.

sentences.zh: 太安初，遣使者二十餘輩循行天下，觀風俗，視民所疾苦。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taian he dispatched more than twenty envoys to tour the realm, observe customs, and look into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taian he sent more than twenty envoys to tour the empire, observe local customs, and investigate the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 詔使者察諸州郡墾殖田畝、飲食衣服、閭里虛實、盜賊劫掠、貧富強劣而罰之，自此牧守頗改前弊，民以安業。

translations.literal: An edict charged the envoys to inspect in all provinces and commanderies reclaimed fields and acreage, food, drink, and clothing, the fullness or emptiness of hamlets and villages, robbery and plunder, and the poor, rich, strong, and weak—and to punish accordingly; from then on pastoral and defending officials largely reformed their former abuses, and the people settled into secure livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys were ordered to inspect reclaimed land, food and clothing, the condition of villages, banditry, and the distribution of wealth and strength—and to punish offenders. From then on governors largely mended their ways, and the people lived in security.

sentences.zh: 自太祖定中原，世祖平方難，收獲珍寶，府藏盈積。

translations.literal: From the time the Taizu pacified the Central Plain and the Shizu quelled difficulties, they gathered treasures and the treasury stores overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: From the Taizu's pacification of the Central Plain through the Shizu's conquest of rival powers, treasures poured in until the treasury overflowed.

sentences.zh: 和平二年秋，詔中尚方作黃金合盤十二具，徑二尺二寸，鏤以白銀，鈿以玫瑰，其銘曰：「九州致貢，殊域來賓，乃作茲器，錯用具珍。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Heping an edict ordered the Central Palace Workshop to make twelve golden covered trays, two feet two inches in diameter, engraved with silver and inlaid with rose quartz; the inscription read: 'The nine provinces present tribute; distant realms come as guests—therefore this vessel is made, inlaid with every treasure.'
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the second year of Heping an edict ordered the imperial workshop to fashion twelve golden covered trays two feet two inches across, engraved in silver and inlaid with rose quartz. The inscription read: 'The nine provinces bring tribute; distant lands send guests—therefore this vessel is wrought, inlaid with every treasure.'

sentences.zh: 鍜以紫金，鏤以白銀，範圍擬載，吐燿含真。

translations.literal: Forged with purple gold, engraved with white silver, its compass modeled on the carriage of heaven, radiating splendor and holding truth within.
translations.idiomatic: Forged in purple gold, engraved in white silver, its compass modeled on the celestial chariot, radiant with splendor and holding truth within.

sentences.zh: 纖文麗質，若化若神，皇王御之，百福惟新。

translations.literal: Fine patterns and beautiful substance, as if transformed, as if divine—the sovereign king who employs it receives a hundred blessings renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Fine patterns and noble substance, seeming transformed, seeming divine—the sovereign who uses it receives a hundred blessings made new.

sentences.zh: 」其年冬，詔出內庫綾綿布帛二十萬匹，令內外百官分曹賭射。

translations.literal: That winter an edict released two hundred thousand bolts of damask silk and cloth from the inner treasury and ordered officials within and without the palace to divide into groups for gambling archery.
translations.idiomatic: That winter an edict released two hundred thousand bolts of damask, silk floss, and cloth from the inner treasury for officials inside and outside the palace to compete at archery by department.

sentences.zh: 四年春，詔賜京師之民年七十已上太官厨食以終其身。

translations.literal: In spring of the fourth year an edict granted the people of the capital aged seventy and above meals from the Grand Provisioner's kitchen for the rest of their lives.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fourth year an edict granted all residents of the capital aged seventy or older meals from the imperial kitchen for life.

sentences.zh: 顯祖即位，親行儉素，率先公卿，思所以賑益黎庶。

translations.literal: When Xianzu acceded to the throne, he personally practiced frugality and simplicity, taking the lead before dukes and ministers, pondering how to relieve and benefit the common people.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzu came to the throne he lived frugally himself, setting an example for the nobility while seeking ways to relieve and benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 至天安、皇興間，歲頻大旱，絹匹千錢。

translations.literal: By the Tianan and Huangxing eras great droughts came year after year; a bolt of silk cost a thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianan and Huangxing eras drought struck year after year, and a bolt of silk cost a thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 劉彧淮北青、冀、徐、兗、司五州告亂請降，命將率眾以援之。

translations.literal: Liu Yu of the five provinces Qing, Ji, Xu, Yan, and Si north of the Huai reported rebellion and sought surrender; he ordered generals to lead troops to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu reported unrest in Qing, Ji, Xu, Yan, and Si—the five provinces north of the Huai—and offered to surrender. The emperor ordered generals to lead troops to their aid.

sentences.zh: 既臨其境，青冀懷貳，進軍圍之，數年乃拔。

translations.literal: Once they reached that territory, Qing and Ji harbored double loyalty; the army advanced and besieged them, and only after several years were they taken.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army arrived, Qing and Ji proved disloyal. The troops advanced, laid siege, and took the cities only after several years.

sentences.zh: 山東之民咸勤於征戍轉運，帝深以為念。

translations.literal: The people east of the mountains all toiled at campaigning, garrison duty, and transport; the emperor was deeply concerned.
translations.idiomatic: The people east of the mountains bore the full burden of campaigning, garrison duty, and transport, and the emperor was deeply troubled on their account.

sentences.zh: 遂因民貧富，為租輸三等九品之制。

translations.literal: Thereupon, according to the people's wealth and poverty, he established a system of rent delivery in three grades and nine ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He then graded rent payments into three tiers and nine ranks according to each household's wealth.

sentences.zh: 千里內納粟，千里外納米；

translations.literal: within a thousand li they paid grain; beyond a thousand li they paid husked rice;
translations.idiomatic: within a thousand li households paid grain; beyond a thousand li they paid husked rice;

sentences.zh: 上三品戶入京師，中三品入他州要倉，下三品入本州。

translations.literal: the upper three ranks delivered to the capital; the middle three ranks to key granaries in other provinces; the lower three ranks to their home province.
translations.idiomatic: the upper three ranks delivered to the capital, the middle three to key granaries in other provinces, and the lower three to their home province.

sentences.zh: 先是太安中，高宗以常賦之外雜調十五，頗為煩重，將與除之。

translations.literal: Previously in the Taian era Gaozong, because miscellaneous levies beyond the regular tax amounted to fifteen items and were quite burdensome, was about to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Taian era, Gaozong found that fifteen miscellaneous levies on top of the regular tax were unduly burdensome and planned to abolish them.

sentences.zh: 尚書毛法仁曰：「此是軍國資用，今頓罷之，臣愚以為不可。

translations.literal: The Minister Mao Faren said: 'These are resources for army and state. To abolish them all at once—in my foolish view this cannot be done.'
translations.idiomatic: Minister Mao Faren said: 'These supplies fund the army and the state. To abolish them all at once would, in my humble view, be unwise.'

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「使地利無窮，民力不竭，百姓有餘，吾孰與不足。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Make the land's benefits inexhaustible and the people's strength unspent; when the common people have surplus, how could I lack?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: 'Let the land yield without end and the people's strength never fail. When the people have plenty, how could I go wanting?'

sentences.zh: 」遂免之。

translations.literal: He thereupon exempted them.
translations.idiomatic: He exempted them nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復調如前，至是乃終罷焉。

translations.literal: Before long the levies were restored as before; only now were they finally abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the levies were restored as before; only now were they abolished for good.

sentences.zh: 於是賦斂稍輕，民復贍矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon taxes and levies grew somewhat lighter and the people were again provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes eased somewhat, and the people were able to live securely again.

sentences.zh: 舊制，民間所織絹、布，皆幅廣二尺二寸，長四十尺為一匹，六十尺為一端，令任服用。

translations.literal: Under the old system, silk and cloth woven by the people were all two feet two inches in width; forty feet made one bolt, sixty feet one end-piece, and these were permitted for clothing at will.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules, household-woven silk and cloth were two feet two inches wide; forty feet constituted one bolt and sixty feet one end-piece, and both were permitted for ordinary dress.

sentences.zh: 後乃漸至濫惡，不依尺度。

translations.literal: Later this gradually declined into shoddy work that did not follow the standard measures.
translations.idiomatic: In time quality declined and the standard measures were widely ignored.

sentences.zh: 高祖延興三年秋七月，更立嚴制，令一準前式，違者罪各有差，有司不檢察與同罪。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the third year of Yanxing of Gaozu, stricter regulations were re-established, requiring all to conform to the former standard; violators received punishments of varying degree, and officials who failed to inspect shared the same guilt.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn in Gaozu's third year of Yanxing, stricter rules were issued requiring full conformity to the old standard. Offenders were punished by degree, and officials who failed to inspect were guilty of the same offense.

sentences.zh: 太和八年，始準古班百官之祿，以品第各有差。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taihe they first followed the ancient regulation of officials' salaries, with differences according to rank and grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taihe salaries for all officials were first set according to ancient precedent, graded by rank.

sentences.zh: 先是，天下戶以九品混通，戶調帛二匹、絮二斤、絲一斤、粟二十石；

translations.literal: Previously, households throughout the realm were assessed in mixed fashion by nine ranks; the household levy was two bolts of silk, two jin of floss, one jin of raw silk, and twenty shi of grain;
translations.idiomatic: Previously households empire-wide were assessed in nine mixed ranks. The household levy was two bolts of silk, two jin of floss, one jin of raw silk, and twenty shi of grain;

sentences.zh: 又入帛一匹二丈，委之州庫，以供調外之費。

translations.literal: in addition they paid one bolt and two zhang of silk, deposited in the provincial treasury to supply expenses beyond the regular levy.
translations.idiomatic: plus one bolt and two zhang of silk deposited in the provincial treasury for expenses beyond the regular levy.

sentences.zh: 至是，戶增帛三匹，粟二石九斗，以為官司之祿。

translations.literal: At this time the household levy was increased by three bolts of silk and two shi nine dou of grain to serve as official salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Now the household levy was increased by three bolts of silk and two shi nine dou of grain to fund official salaries.

sentences.zh: 後增調外帛滿二匹。

translations.literal: Later the silk beyond the regular levy was increased to a full two bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Later the supplemental levy was raised to a full two bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 所調各隨其土所出。

translations.literal: Each levy followed what the local soil produced.
translations.idiomatic: Each levy was paid in whatever the local region produced.

sentences.zh: 其司、冀、雍、華、定、相、泰、[2]洛、豫、懷、兗、陝、徐、青、齊、濟、南豫、東兗、東徐十九州，貢綿絹及絲；

translations.literal: the nineteen provinces of Si, Ji, Yong, Hua, Ding, Xiang, Tai, Luo, Yu, Huai, Yan, Shan, Xu, Qing, Qi, Ji, Southern Yu, Eastern Yan, and Eastern Xu paid floss silk, damask, and raw silk;
translations.idiomatic: the nineteen provinces of Si, Ji, Yong, Hua, Ding, Xiang, Tai, Luo, Yu, Huai, Yan, Shan, Xu, Qing, Qi, Ji, Southern Yu, Eastern Yan, and Eastern Xu paid floss silk, damask, and raw silk;

sentences.zh: 幽、平、并、肆、岐、涇、荊、涼、梁、汾、秦、安、營、豳、夏、光、郢、東秦，司州萬年、雁門、上谷、靈丘、廣寧、平涼郡，懷州邵上郡之長平、白水縣，[3]青州北海郡之膠東縣、平昌郡之東武平昌縣、高密郡之昌安高密夷安黔陬縣，泰州河東之蒲坂、汾陰縣，東徐州東莞郡之莒、諸、東莞縣，雍州馮翊郡之蓮芍縣、[4]咸陽郡之寧夷縣、北地郡之三原雲陽銅官宜君縣，華州華山郡之夏陽縣，徐州北濟陰郡之離狐豐縣、[5]東海郡之贛榆襄賁縣，皆以麻布充稅。

translations.literal: You, Ping, Bing, Si, Qi, Jing, Jing, Liang, Liang, Fen, Qin, An, Ying, Bin, Xia, Guang, Ying, and Eastern Qin, together with the commanderies of Wannian, Yanmen, Shanggu, Lingqiu, Guangning, and Pingliang in Si Province; Changping and Baishui counties in Shaoshang Commandery of Huai Province; Jiaodong County in Beihai Commandery of Qing Province; Dongwu and Pingchang counties in Pingchang Commandery; Chang'an, Gaomi, Yi'an, and Qianqiu counties in Gaomi Commandery; Puban and Fenyin counties in Hedong of Tai Province; Ju, Zhu, and Dongguan counties in Dongguan Commandery of Eastern Xu Province; Lianjue County in Fengyi Commandery of Yong Province; Ningyi County in Xianyang Commandery; Sanyuan, Yunyang, Tongguan, and Yijun counties in Beidi Commandery; Xiayang County in Huashan Commandery of Hua Province; Lihu and Feng counties in Northern Jiyin Commandery of Xu Province; and Ganyu and Xiangben counties in Donghai Commandery—all paid tax in hemp cloth.
translations.idiomatic: You, Ping, Bing, Si, Qi, Jing, Liang, Fen, Qin, An, Ying, Bin, Xia, Guang, Ying, and Eastern Qin, together with Wannian, Yanmen, Shanggu, Lingqiu, Guangning, and Pingliang in Si Province; Changping and Baishui in Shaoshang of Huai Province; Jiaodong in Beihai of Qing Province; Dongwu and Pingchang in Pingchang Commandery; Chang'an, Gaomi, Yi'an, and Qianqiu in Gaomi Commandery; Puban and Fenyin in Hedong of Tai Province; Ju, Zhu, and Dongguan in Dongguan of Eastern Xu Province; Lianjue in Fengyi of Yong Province; Ningyi in Xianyang; Sanyuan, Yunyang, Tongguan, and Yijun in Beidi; Xiayang in Huashan of Hua Province; Lihu and Feng in Northern Jiyin of Xu Province; and Ganyu and Xiangben in Donghai—all paid their levies in hemp cloth.

sentences.zh: 九年，下詔均給天下民田：

translations.literal: In the ninth year an edict was issued to distribute farmland equally to the people throughout the realm:
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year an edict ordered equal distribution of farmland to the people throughout the realm:

sentences.zh: 諸男夫十五以上，受露田四十畝，[6]婦人二十畝，奴婢依良。

translations.literal: All adult males aged fifteen and above received forty mu of open-field land; women received twenty mu; slaves and servants followed free persons.
translations.idiomatic: Every adult male aged fifteen or older received forty mu of open-field land; women received twenty mu; and slaves and servants were allotted land on the same terms as free persons.

sentences.zh: 丁牛一頭受田三十畝，限四牛。

translations.literal: Each draft ox received thirty mu, with a limit of four oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Each draft ox received thirty mu, up to a maximum of four oxen per household.

sentences.zh: 所授之田率倍之，三易之田再倍之，以供耕作及還受之盈縮。

translations.literal: The land granted was generally doubled; land requiring rotation every three years was doubled again, to supply cultivation and the surplus or shortfall in returns and re-allotments.
translations.idiomatic: Granted land was generally doubled in area; fields requiring rotation every three years were doubled again, to allow for cultivation and for surplus or shortfall when land was returned and re-allotted.

sentences.zh: 諸民年及課則受田，老免及身沒則還田。

translations.literal: When the people reached taxable age they received land; upon old-age exemption or death the land was returned.
translations.idiomatic: People received land when they reached taxable age and returned it upon reaching old-age exemption or at death.

sentences.zh: 奴婢、牛隨有無以還受。

translations.literal: Slaves, servants, and oxen were returned or received according to whether they were present or absent.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves, servants, and oxen were allotted or returned according to whether the household had them.

sentences.zh: 諸桑田不在還受之限，但通入倍田分。

translations.literal: All mulberry fields lay outside the limits of return and receipt, but were counted together into the doubled-field allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberry fields were not subject to return and re-allotment but were counted toward the doubled-field quota.

sentences.zh: 於分雖盈，沒則還田，不得以充露田之數。

translations.literal: Though the allotment might be in surplus, upon death the land was returned and could not be counted toward open-field quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the allotment exceeded the quota, the land was returned at death and could not be counted toward open-field allotments.

sentences.zh: [7]不足者以露田充倍。

translations.literal: Where there was shortfall, open-field land made up the doubled portion.
translations.idiomatic: Shortfalls were made up with open-field land counted toward the doubled allotment.

sentences.zh: 諸初受田者，男夫一人給田二十畝，課蒔餘，種桑五十樹，棗五株，榆三根。

translations.literal: For all who first received land, each adult male was given twenty mu, taxed for planting surplus crops, and required to plant fifty mulberry trees, five jujube trees, and three elm trees.
translations.idiomatic: Those receiving land for the first time were allotted twenty mu per adult male, taxed on surplus planting, and required to plant fifty mulberry trees, five jujube trees, and three elms.

sentences.zh: 非桑之土，夫給一畝，依法課蒔榆、棗。

translations.literal: On land unsuited to mulberries, each male was given one mu and taxed by law to plant elms and jujubes.
translations.idiomatic: On land unsuited to mulberries, each male received one mu and was required by law to plant elms and jujubes.

sentences.zh: 奴各依良。

translations.literal: Slaves each followed free persons.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves followed the same rules as free persons.

sentences.zh: 限三年種畢，不畢，奪其不畢之地。

translations.literal: A limit of three years was set to finish planting; if not finished, the unplanted land was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Planting had to be completed within three years; otherwise the unplanted land was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 於桑榆地分雜蒔餘果及多種桑榆者不禁。

translations.literal: Within the mulberry and elm allotments, interplanting other fruits and planting extra mulberry and elm were not forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Within mulberry and elm allotments, interplanting other fruit trees and planting extra mulberry and elm were permitted.

sentences.zh: 諸應還之田，不得種桑榆棗果，種者以違令論，地入還分。

translations.literal: On all land due to be returned, mulberry, elm, jujube, and fruit trees might not be planted; planters were prosecuted for violating the order and the land entered the return allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Land due to be returned could not be planted with mulberry, elm, jujube, or fruit trees. Violators were punished and the land reverted to the return pool.

sentences.zh: 諸桑田皆為世業，身終不還，恒從見口。

translations.literal: All mulberry fields were hereditary estates, never returned at death, always following the present household members.
translations.idiomatic: All mulberry fields were hereditary property, never returned at death, and always passed with the living members of the household.

sentences.zh: 有盈者無受無還，不足者受種如法。

translations.literal: Those with surplus received nothing and returned nothing; those with shortfall received planting allotments according to the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Households with surplus received no additional land and returned none; those with shortfall received planting allotments according to the rules.

sentences.zh: 盈者得賣其盈，不足者得買所不足。

translations.literal: Those with surplus might sell the surplus; those with shortfall might buy what they lacked.
translations.idiomatic: Households with surplus could sell the excess; those with shortfall could buy what they needed.

sentences.zh: 不得賣其分，亦不得買過所足。

translations.literal: They might not sell their allotted share, nor buy beyond what was sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: They could not sell their allotted quota, nor buy more than their allotment required.

sentences.zh: 諸麻布之土，男夫及課，別給麻田十畝，婦人五畝，奴婢依良。

translations.literal: In all hemp-cloth regions, adult males of taxable age were separately given ten mu of hemp fields, women five mu, and slaves and servants followed free persons.
translations.idiomatic: In hemp-producing regions, each taxable adult male received ten mu of hemp fields and each woman five mu; slaves and servants followed the same rules as free persons.

sentences.zh: 皆從還受之法。

translations.literal: All followed the law of return and receipt.
translations.idiomatic: All of this was subject to the rules governing return and re-allotment of land.

sentences.zh: 諸有舉戶老小癃殘無授田者，年十一已上及癃者各授以半夫田，年踰七十者不還所受，寡婦守志者雖免課亦授婦田。

translations.literal: For all households with only old, young, debilitated, or disabled members who received no land allotment, those eleven years and above and the debilitated each received half a male's allotment; those over seventy did not return what they had received; widows who maintained chastity, though exempt from tax, still received woman's field allotments.
translations.idiomatic: Households consisting only of the old, young, infirm, or disabled with no land allotments were granted half a male's quota to each person aged eleven or above and to each disabled person. Those over seventy kept their allotments without returning them. Widows who remained chaste, though exempt from tax, still received woman's field allotments.

sentences.zh: 諸還受民田，恒以正月。

translations.literal: The return and receipt of civilian land always took place in the first month.
translations.idiomatic: Return and re-allotment of civilian land always took place in the first month of the year.

sentences.zh: 若始受田而身亡，及賣買奴婢牛者，皆至明年正月乃得還受。

translations.literal: If one died upon first receiving land, or if slaves, servants, or oxen were bought or sold, return and receipt waited until the first month of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: If someone died upon first receiving land, or if slaves, servants, or oxen were bought or sold, land was not returned and re-allotted until the first month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 諸土廣民稀之處，隨力所及，官借民種蒔。

translations.literal: In all regions where land was vast and people sparse, as far as strength permitted, the government lent seed to the people for planting.
translations.idiomatic: In regions of abundant land and sparse population, the government lent seed for planting as far as local capacity allowed.

sentences.zh: 役有土居者，[8]依法封授。

translations.literal: Those performing corvée labor who owned residential land were, [8] by law, granted sealed allotments.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée laborers who owned residential land [8] received formal allotments under the law.

sentences.zh: 諸地狹之處，有進丁受田而不樂遷者，則以其家桑田為正田分，又不足不給倍田，又不足家內人別減分。

translations.literal: In all regions where land was narrow, if an adult son coming of age received land but was unwilling to relocate, then the household's mulberry fields served as the regular field allotment; if still insufficient, no doubled fields were given; if still insufficient, each person within the household had their share reduced separately.
translations.idiomatic: In densely settled regions, if a newly adult son received land but refused to relocate, the household's mulberry fields counted as their regular field allotment. If that was still insufficient, no doubled fields were granted; if still insufficient, each household member's share was reduced accordingly.

sentences.zh: 無桑之鄉準此為法。

translations.literal: Districts without mulberries took this as their standard.
translations.idiomatic: Districts without mulberry cultivation followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 樂遷者聽逐空荒，不限異州他郡，唯不聽避勞就逸。

translations.literal: Those willing to relocate were permitted to follow vacant and wasteland, without restriction to other provinces or commanderies; only avoidance of labor for ease was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those willing to relocate might settle on vacant or abandoned land anywhere, across provinces and commanderies, but they were not permitted to shirk labor for an easier life.

sentences.zh: 其地足之處，不得無故而移。

translations.literal: Where land was adequate, removal without cause was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In regions where land was sufficient, relocation without good cause was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸民有新居者，三口給地一畝，以為居室，奴婢五口給一畝。

translations.literal: For all people with new residences, three persons received one mu of land as living quarters; five slaves or servants received one mu.
translations.idiomatic: Newly settled households received one mu of residential land for every three persons and one mu for every five slaves or servants.

sentences.zh: 男女十五以上，因其地分，口課種菜五分畝之一。

translations.literal: Males and females fifteen years and above, according to their land allotment, were taxed five-tenths of one mu per person for growing vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women aged fifteen or above were taxed at half a mu per person for vegetable planting, based on their land allotment.

sentences.zh: 諸一人之分，正從正，倍從倍，不得隔越他畔。

translations.literal: For each person's allotment, regular fields followed regular fields and doubled fields followed doubled fields; crossing into another's boundary was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Each person's allotment had to keep regular and doubled fields separate; no one could encroach on another's boundaries.

sentences.zh: 進丁受田者恒從所近。

translations.literal: Those coming of age and receiving land always received it from what was nearest.
translations.idiomatic: Newly adult sons received land from the nearest available plots.

sentences.zh: 若同時俱受，先貧後富。

translations.literal: If received at the same time, the poor came first and the rich afterward.
translations.idiomatic: When allotments were made simultaneously, poor households received land before wealthy ones.

sentences.zh: 再倍之田，放此為法。

translations.literal: For land allotted at double or redouble rates, this served as the rule.
translations.idiomatic: The same rules applied to double and redouble allotments.

sentences.zh: 諸遠流配謫、無子孫、及戶絕者，墟宅、桑榆盡為公田，以供授受。

translations.literal: For all exiled to distant places, those without descendants, and households extinct, ruined dwellings, mulberry trees, and elms all became public land for allotment and receipt.
translations.idiomatic: Land from exiles, households without descendants, and extinct families—including abandoned dwellings, mulberries, and elms—reverted to public land for re-allotment.

sentences.zh: 授受之次，給其所親；

translations.literal: in the order of allotment and receipt, it was given to their relatives;
translations.idiomatic: when re-allotting, it went first to their relatives;

sentences.zh: 未給之間，亦借其所親。

translations.literal: before it was allotted, it was also lent to their relatives.
translations.idiomatic: pending allotment, it could be lent to those relatives.

sentences.zh: 諸宰民之官，各隨地給公田，[9]刺史十五頃，太守十頃，治中別駕各八頃，縣令、郡丞六頃。

translations.literal: All officials who governed the people, according to their locality, were given public fields: [9] provincial inspector fifteen qing, commandery administrator ten qing, aides and deputy administrators each eight qing, magistrate and commandery assistant six qing.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials received salary land according to rank:[9] provincial inspectors fifteen qing, commandery administrators ten qing, aides and deputy administrators eight qing each, and county magistrates and commandery assistants six qing.

sentences.zh: 更代相付。

translations.literal: Successive replacements handed them over to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Successors passed the land to their replacements upon taking office.

sentences.zh: 賣者坐如律。

translations.literal: Sellers were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who sold such land was punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 魏初不立三長，故民多蔭附。

translations.literal: In the early Wei no three-heads system was established, so the people widely sought patronage attachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wei, because the three-heads system had not been established, many people placed themselves under powerful patrons.

sentences.zh: 蔭附者皆無官役，豪強徵斂，倍於公賦。

translations.literal: Those under patronage attachment owed no official corvée; powerful families levied collections more than double the public tax.
translations.idiomatic: Patronage clients were exempt from official corvée, but strong households extracted levies more than double the state's tax burden.

sentences.zh: 十年，給事中李沖上言：「宜準古，五家立一隣長，五隣立一里長，五里立一黨長，長取鄉人強謹者。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Attendant Within the Yellow Gates Li Chong submitted a memorial: "One should follow antiquity: five households establish one neighborhood head; five neighborhoods one hamlet head; five hamlets one ward head. Heads should be taken from strong and conscientious men of the community."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Attendant Within the Yellow Gates Li Chong submitted a memorial: "We should follow ancient practice: appoint a neighborhood head for every five households, a hamlet head for every five neighborhoods, and a ward head for every five hamlets, selecting strong and conscientious local men."

sentences.zh: 隣長復一夫，里長二，黨長三。

translations.literal: The neighborhood head was exempt for one male, the hamlet head for two, the ward head for three.
translations.idiomatic: Neighborhood heads received exemption for one adult male, hamlet heads for two, and ward heads for three.

sentences.zh: 所復復征戍，餘若民。

translations.literal: What was exempted was again subject to campaigning and garrison duty; the remainder was as for ordinary people.
translations.idiomatic: The exempt males still owed military campaigning and garrison duty; all other obligations remained as for ordinary subjects.

sentences.zh: 三載亡愆則陟用，陟之一等。

translations.literal: After three years without fault they were promoted and appointed, promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: After three years without misconduct, they were promoted and appointed one rank higher.

sentences.zh: 其民調，一夫一婦帛一匹，粟二石。

translations.literal: The civilian household levy was one bolt of silk per male-female pair, and two shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: The household levy was one bolt of silk and two shi of grain per adult couple.

sentences.zh: 民年十五以上未娶者，四人出一夫一婦之調；

translations.literal: For people fifteen or above who were unmarried, four persons contributed one male-female pair's levy;
translations.idiomatic: unmarried men aged fifteen or above contributed one couple's levy for every four persons;

sentences.zh: 奴任耕，婢任績者，八口當未娶者四；

translations.literal: slaves assigned to farming or maidservants assigned to weaving counted as four unmarried persons for every eight;
translations.idiomatic: eight farming slaves or weaving maidservants counted as four unmarried men;

sentences.zh: 耕牛二十頭當奴婢八。

translations.literal: twenty oxen used for plowing counted as eight slaves or servants.
translations.idiomatic: twenty plow oxen counted as eight slaves or servants.

sentences.zh: 其麻布之鄉，一夫一婦布一匹，下至牛，以此為降。

translations.literal: In hemp-cloth districts, one bolt of cloth per male-female pair, scaled down to oxen by the same principle.
translations.idiomatic: In hemp-producing regions, each couple paid one bolt of cloth, with reductions scaled down through unmarried men, slaves, and oxen by the same ratios.

sentences.zh: 大率十匹為公調，[10]二匹為調外費，三匹為內外百官俸，此外雜調。

translations.literal: Roughly, ten bolts were the public levy, [10] two bolts supplementary levy expenses, three bolts salaries for officials inside and outside, and beyond these miscellaneous levies.
translations.idiomatic: In general, ten bolts went to the public levy,[10] two to supplementary expenses, three to salaries for officials at court and in the provinces, with miscellaneous levies beyond these.

sentences.zh: 民年八十已上，聽一子不從役。

translations.literal: For people eighty years and above, one son was permitted not to perform corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Households with members aged eighty or above were permitted to exempt one son from corvée duty.

sentences.zh: 孤獨癃老篤疾貧窮不能自存者，三長內迭養食之。」

translations.literal: The orphaned, solitary, debilitated, aged, severely ill, and poor who could not sustain themselves were to be fed in rotation within the three-heads system."
translations.idiomatic: Orphans, the solitary, the infirm, the aged, the seriously ill, and the destitute who could not support themselves were to be fed in rotation by the three-heads organization."

sentences.zh: 書奏，諸官通議，稱善者眾。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, officials discussed it jointly and many praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, officials held a joint discussion and the praise was widespread.

sentences.zh: 高祖從之，於是遣使者行其事。

translations.literal: Gaozu followed it, and thereupon dispatched envoys to carry out the measure.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu accepted it and dispatched envoys to implement the reform.

sentences.zh: 乃詔曰：「夫任土錯貢，所以通有無；

translations.literal: Then an edict said: "Matching tribute to the land's products is how abundance and want are joined;
translations.idiomatic: Then an edict proclaimed: "Assigning tribute according to local products is how surplus and shortage are balanced;

sentences.zh: 井乘定賦，所以均勞逸。

translations.literal: fixing levies by well and mulberry land is how labor and ease are equalized.
translations.idiomatic: setting levies by household and land is how burdens of labor and leisure are equalized.

sentences.zh: 有無通則民財不匱，勞逸均則人樂其業。

translations.literal: When abundance and want are joined the people's wealth is not exhausted; when labor and ease are equalized people delight in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: When surplus and shortage are balanced the people's wealth does not fail; when labor and leisure are equalized the people find contentment in their work.

sentences.zh: 此自古之常道也。

translations.literal: This has been the constant way since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: This has been the constant principle since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 又隣里鄉黨之制，所由來久。

translations.literal: Moreover, the system of neighborhoods, hamlets, and wards has long existed.
translations.idiomatic: The system of neighborhoods, hamlets, and wards, moreover, has existed since long ago.

sentences.zh: 欲使風教易周，家至日見，以大督小，從近及遠，如身之使手，幹之總條，然後口算平均，義興訟息。

translations.literal: It is intended to make customs and instruction easy to spread comprehensively, reaching every household daily; to supervise the small through the great, from near to far, like the body commanding the hand or the branches commanding the twigs; only then are per-capita assessments even and righteousness flourishes while litigation ceases.
translations.idiomatic: It is meant to spread customs and instruction to every household, to govern the small through the great and the near through the far, as the body directs the hand and the trunk commands the branches—so that per-capita assessments are fair, virtue rises, and lawsuits cease.

sentences.zh: 是以三典所同，隨世洿隆；

translations.literal: Thus the Three Canons agree on it, rising and falling with the age;
translations.idiomatic: The Three Canons alike attest to this, adapting to the rise and fall of the times;

sentences.zh: 貳監之行，從時損益。

translations.literal: the conduct of the assistant overseers was adjusted according to the times.
translations.idiomatic: and the work of the supervising officials has been adjusted to suit each age.

sentences.zh: 故鄭僑復丘賦之術，鄒人獻盍徹之規。

translations.literal: Therefore Zichan of Zheng restored the mound-levy method, and men of Zou presented the proposal of why-not-tithe.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zichan of Zheng restored the mound-levy method, and men of Zou offered the proposal to abolish the tithe.

sentences.zh: 雖輕重不同，而當時俱適。

translations.literal: Though light and heavy differed, each suited its time.
translations.idiomatic: Though the burdens differed in weight, each suited its own age.

sentences.zh: 自昔以來，諸州戶口，籍貫不實，包藏隱漏，廢公罔私。

translations.literal: From old, household registers in the provinces were inaccurate in nativity; concealment and leakage hid subjects and betrayed the public for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: For generations, provincial household registers have been false; concealment and evasion have cheated the state and served private interest.

sentences.zh: 富強者并兼有餘，貧弱者餬口不足。

translations.literal: The powerful combined and held surplus; the weak scraped insufficient mouthsful.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful amassed more than they needed while the weak could barely feed themselves.

sentences.zh: 賦稅齊等，無輕重之殊；

translations.literal: taxes and levies were equal without distinction of light and heavy;
translations.idiomatic: taxes were levied equally, with no distinction between rich and poor;

sentences.zh: 力役同科，無眾寡之別。

translations.literal: labor corvée was the same category without distinction of many or few.
translations.idiomatic: corvée fell equally on all, with no regard for household size.

sentences.zh: 雖建九品之格，而豐埆之土未融；

translations.literal: though the nine-rank scheme was established, fertile and sterile lands were not harmonized;
translations.idiomatic: though the nine-rank scheme was established, fertile and barren lands were not treated alike;

sentences.zh: 雖立均輸之楷，而蠶績之鄉無異。

translations.literal: though the even-transport standard was established, silk-weaving districts were not differentiated.
translations.idiomatic: though the even-transport standard was set, silk-producing regions were taxed no differently.

sentences.zh: 致使淳化未樹，民情偷薄。

translations.literal: This caused pure transformation not to be planted and popular sentiment to grow grasping and thin.
translations.idiomatic: Pure custom has failed to take root, and popular morals have grown lax and grasping.

sentences.zh: 朕每思之，良懷深慨。

translations.literal: I think on this always and deeply sigh in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I reflect on this, I am deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 今革舊從新，為里黨之法，在所牧守，宜以喻民，使知去煩即簡之要。

translations.literal: Now, reforming the old and following the new, establishing the law of hamlets and wards, the local governors and prefects should explain it to the people so they know the essentials of leaving trouble and embracing simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Now, in reforming the old and adopting the new and establishing the hamlet-and-ward system, local governors and prefects should explain it to the people so they understand the principle of casting off burdens and embracing simplicity.

sentences.zh: 」初，百姓咸以為不若循常，豪富并兼者尤弗願也。

translations.literal: At first the common people all thought it inferior to following custom, and the powerful who combined holdings were especially unwilling.
translations.idiomatic: At first the common people all believed the new system inferior to the old ways, and powerful landlords who had combined holdings were especially unwilling.

sentences.zh: 事施行後，計省昔十有餘倍。

translations.literal: After the measure was implemented, calculations showed savings of more than ten times compared with before.
translations.idiomatic: Once the reform was implemented, administrative costs fell to less than a tenth of what they had been.

sentences.zh: 於是海內安之。

translations.literal: Thereupon peace settled throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the realm was at peace.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大旱，京都民飢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, great drought; the people of the capital starved.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year a great drought struck, and the people of the capital went hungry.

sentences.zh: 加以牛疫，公私闕乏，時有以馬驢及橐駝供駕輓耕載。

translations.literal: Added to this was cattle plague; public and private stores were depleted; at times horses, donkeys, and camels were used for carriage, traction, plowing, and transport.
translations.idiomatic: Cattle plague compounded the crisis; public and private supplies ran short, and horses, donkeys, and camels were pressed into service for transport, plowing, and hauling.

sentences.zh: 詔聽民就豐。

translations.literal: An edict permitted the people to go where harvests were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted the people to migrate to regions where harvests were abundant.

sentences.zh: 行者十五六，道路給糧稟，至所在，三長贍養之。

translations.literal: Of those who traveled, five or six in ten; the road provided grain rations; upon arrival the three-heads organization fed them.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly half to three-fifths of the people migrated; grain rations were provided on the road, and upon arrival the three-heads organization supplied their sustenance.

sentences.zh: 遣使者時省察焉。

translations.literal: Envoys were dispatched to inspect periodically.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched envoys to inspect the situation periodically.

sentences.zh: 留業者，皆令主司審覈，開倉賑貸。

translations.literal: Those who remained were all ordered by responsible offices to examine and verify, opening granaries for relief loans.
translations.idiomatic: Those who remained were registered by local authorities, and granaries were opened to provide relief grain on loan.

sentences.zh: 其有特不自存者，悉檢集，為粥於術衢，以救其困。

translations.literal: Those especially unable to sustain themselves were all gathered, and congee was made on the main roads to rescue their distress.
translations.idiomatic: Those utterly unable to support themselves were gathered and fed congee at major crossroads to relieve their distress.

sentences.zh: 然主者不明牧察，郊甸間甚多餧死者。

translations.literal: Yet the responsible officials did not clearly shepherd and inspect; in the outskirts many died of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet local officials failed to supervise relief properly, and many starved to death in the capital outskirts.

sentences.zh: 時承平日久，府藏盈積，詔盡出御府衣服珍寶、太官雜器、太僕乘具、內庫弓矢刀鉾十分之八、外府衣物繒布絲纊諸所供國用者，以其太半班齎百司，下至工商皂隸，逮于六鎮邊戍，畿內鰥寡孤獨貧癃者，皆有差。

translations.literal: As peace had long prevailed and treasury stores overflowed, an edict ordered that all imperial robes and treasures, kitchen utensils, carriage fittings from the Director of Imperial Studs, eight-tenths of bows, arrows, blades, and halberds from the inner storehouse, and clothing, silk, hemp, and all other supplies from the outer treasury be distributed—more than half to the hundred offices, down to artisans, merchants, and menials, reaching the six frontier garrisons and border posts, and the widowed, orphaned, solitary, poor, and infirm within the capital region, each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had long prevailed and the treasuries were full, so an edict ordered the distribution of imperial robes and treasures, kitchen utensils, carriage fittings from the Director of Imperial Studs, eight-tenths of the bows, arrows, blades, and halberds from the inner armory, and clothing, silk, hemp, and all other state supplies from the outer treasury—more than half to the hundred offices, down to artisans, merchants, and menials, reaching the six frontier garrisons and border posts, and the widowed, orphaned, solitary, poor, and infirm within the capital region, each according to rank.

sentences.zh: 十二年，詔羣臣求安民之術。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, an edict ordered the ministers to seek methods to secure the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year an edict ordered the ministers to propose measures for securing the people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 有司上言：「請析州郡常調九分之二，京都度支歲用之餘，各立官司，豐年糴貯於倉，時儉則加私之一，糶之於民。

translations.literal: The responsible offices submitted a memorial: "We request that two-ninths of the regular levies from provinces and commanderies, and the surplus from the capital's annual expenditures, each be placed under separate offices; in years of abundance grain should be purchased and stored in granaries, and in years of scarcity it should be sold to the people at one-tenth above cost."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices submitted a memorial: "We propose that two-ninths of the regular levies from provinces and commanderies, together with the surplus from the capital's annual budget, each be placed under separate offices; in years of abundance grain should be purchased and stored in granaries, and in years of scarcity sold to the people at a markup of one-tenth."

sentences.zh: [11]如此，民必力田以買絹，積財以取粟。

translations.literal: [11] Thus the people will surely labor in the fields to buy silk and accumulate wealth to obtain grain.
translations.idiomatic: [11] In this way the people will be compelled to work the fields to earn silk and save grain for lean years.

sentences.zh: 官，年登則常積，歲凶則直給。

translations.literal: For the state, in years of plenty stores will accumulate; in years of famine supplies will be dispensed directly.
translations.idiomatic: The state will accumulate stores in good years and dispense grain directly in bad years.

sentences.zh: 又別立農官，取州郡戶十分之一，以為屯民。

translations.literal: Separate agricultural offices should also be established, taking one-tenth of households from each province and commandery as garrison colonists.
translations.idiomatic: Separate agricultural offices should also be established, drafting one-tenth of households from each province and commandery as garrison colonists.

sentences.zh: 相水陸之宜，斷頃畝之數，以贓贖雜物市牛科給，令其肆力。

translations.literal: Choosing sites suited to water and land, fixing acreage quotas, oxen should be purchased with fines and confiscated goods and distributed by schedule, and the colonists made to exert their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Sites suited to water and land should be chosen, acreage quotas fixed, oxen purchased with fines and confiscated goods and distributed on schedule, and the colonists put to full labor.

sentences.zh: 一夫之田，歲責六十斛，甄其正課并征戍雜役。

translations.literal: For each male's fields, sixty shi of grain were required annually, assessing regular tax together with campaigning, garrison, and miscellaneous corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Each colonist's fields were assessed at sixty shi of grain per year, inclusive of regular tax, military campaigning, garrison duty, and miscellaneous corvée.

sentences.zh: 行此二事，數年之中則穀積而民足矣。

translations.literal: Implementing these two measures, within several years grain would accumulate and the people would be provided for.
translations.idiomatic: If these two measures were implemented, within a few years grain stores would fill and the people would be secure.

sentences.zh: 」帝覽而善之，尋施行焉。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and approved, and soon it was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the proposal and approved it, and it was soon put into effect.

sentences.zh: 自此公私豐贍，雖時有水旱，不為災也。

translations.literal: From this time public and private stores were abundant; though drought and flood occurred from time to time, they did not become disasters.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter both public and private stores were abundant; though drought and flood occurred from time to time, they no longer brought disaster.

sentences.zh: 世宗延昌三年春，有司奏長安驪山有銀鑛，二石得銀七兩。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Yanxing of Emperor Shizong, the responsible offices reported that at Mount Li near Chang'an there was a silver mine yielding seven liang of silver from two shi of ore.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Yanxing under Emperor Shizong, the responsible offices reported a silver mine at Mount Li near Chang'an yielding seven liang of silver from two shi of ore.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，恒州又上言，白登山有銀鑛，八石得銀七兩，錫三百餘斤，其色潔白，有踰上品。

translations.literal: That autumn, Heng Province also reported that Mount Bai near Pingcheng had a silver mine yielding seven liang of silver from eight shi of ore and more than three hundred jin of tin, white and lustrous, surpassing the highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Heng Province also reported a silver mine at Mount Bai near Pingcheng yielding seven liang of silver from eight shi of ore and more than three hundred jin of tin, white and lustrous, surpassing the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 詔並置銀官，常令採鑄。

translations.literal: An edict ordered silver offices established at both sites for continuous mining and smelting.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered silver offices established at both sites for continuous mining and smelting.

sentences.zh: 又漢中舊有金戶千餘家，常於漢水沙淘金，年終總輸。

translations.literal: In Hanzhong there had formerly been more than a thousand gold households who regularly panned gold from the Han River sands and delivered the total at year's end.
translations.idiomatic: In Hanzhong more than a thousand gold-panning households had formerly worked the sands of the Han River and delivered the year's total at year's end.

sentences.zh: 後臨淮王彧為梁州刺史，奏罷之。

translations.literal: Later Prince Linhuai Yu submitted a memorial as Governor of Liang Province to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Linhuai Yu, as Governor of Liang Province, submitted a memorial to abolish them.

sentences.zh: 其鑄鐵為農器、兵刃，在所有之，然以相州牽口冶為工，故常鍊鍛為刀，送於武庫。

translations.literal: Iron was cast into farm tools and weapons everywhere such offices existed, but because the Qian Kou smeltery in Xiang Province was the chief workshop, blades were regularly forged and sent to the arsenal.
translations.idiomatic: Iron was cast into farm tools and weapons wherever such offices existed, but because the Qian Kou smeltery in Xiang Province was the chief workshop, blades were regularly forged there and sent to the arsenal.

sentences.zh: 自魏德既廣，西域、東夷貢其珍物，充於王府。

translations.literal: Once Wei's virtue extended far, the Western Regions and Eastern Yi sent their precious goods to fill the imperial storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei's power extended far, the Western Regions and Eastern Yi sent precious tribute to fill the imperial storehouse.

sentences.zh: 又於南垂立互市，以致南貨，羽毛齒革之屬無遠不至。

translations.literal: Markets for mutual trade were also established on the southern frontier to obtain southern goods; feathers, ivory, and hides arrived from the farthest reaches.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual-trade markets were also established on the southern frontier to obtain southern goods; feathers, ivory, and hides arrived from the farthest reaches.

sentences.zh: 神龜、正光之際，府藏盈溢。

translations.literal: During the Shengui and Zhengguang eras, the treasuries overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengui and Zhengguang eras the treasuries overflowed.

sentences.zh: 靈太后曾令公卿已下任力負物而取之，又數賚禁內左右，所費無貲，而不能一丐百姓也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling once ordered officials from the duke down to carry loads according to their strength and take what they could; she also repeatedly bestowed gifts on those within the inner palace, spending without limit, yet could not give even a single bowl of gruel to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling once ordered officials from the rank of duke downward to carry loads according to their strength and take what they could; she also repeatedly bestowed gifts on those within the inner palace, spending without limit, yet could not spare even a bowl of gruel for the common people.

sentences.zh: 自徐揚內附之後，仍世經略江淮，於是轉運中州，以實邊鎮，百姓疲於道路。

translations.literal: After Xu and Yang submitted, successive generations pressed campaigns along the Huai and Yang, and grain from the central provinces was transported to supply the frontier garrisons, exhausting the people on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu and Yang submitted, successive campaigns along the Huai and Yang required transporting grain from the central provinces to supply the frontier garrisons, exhausting the people on the roads.

sentences.zh: 乃令番戍之兵，營起屯田，又收內郡兵資與民和糴，積為邊備。

translations.literal: Rotational garrison troops were then ordered to establish military colonies, and military provisions from the inner commanderies were collected to purchase grain jointly with the people, accumulating stores for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: Rotational garrison troops were then ordered to establish military colonies, and military provisions from the inner commanderies were used to purchase grain jointly with the people, building up frontier reserves.

sentences.zh: 有司又請於水運之次，隨便置倉，乃於小平、石門、[12]白馬津、漳涯、黑水、濟州、陳郡、大梁凡八所，各立邸閣，每軍國有須，應機漕引。

translations.literal: The responsible offices also requested that granaries be placed conveniently along water transport routes; at Xiaoping, Shimen, [12] White Horse Ford, the Zhang River bank, Blackwater, Jizhou, Chen Commandery, and Daliang—eight sites in all—depots were established, so that whenever army and state had need, grain could be transported and drawn as required.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices also requested granaries along water transport routes; at Xiaoping, Shimen, [12] White Horse Ford, the Zhang River bank, Blackwater, Jizhou, Chen Commandery, and Daliang—eight sites in all—depots were established so that whenever the army or state had need, grain could be transported and drawn as required.

sentences.zh: 自此費役微省。

translations.literal: From this time expenditures and corvée were slightly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter transport costs and corvée labor were somewhat reduced.

sentences.zh: 三門都將薛欽上言：「計京西水次汾華二州、恒農、河北、河東、正平、平陽五郡年常綿絹及貲麻皆折公物，雇車牛送京。

translations.literal: Commandant of Sanmen Xue Qin submitted a memorial: "It is calculated that the two provinces of Fen and Hua west of the capital, and the five commanderies of Hengnong, Hebei, Hedong, Zhengping, and Pingyang, annually deliver silk and hemp as public goods, hiring carts and oxen to transport them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Sanmen Xue Qin submitted a memorial: "It is calculated that the two provinces of Fen and Hua west of the capital and the five commanderies of Hengnong, Hebei, Hedong, Zhengping, and Pingyang annually deliver silk and hemp as public goods, hiring carts and oxen to transport them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 道險人弊，費公損私。

translations.literal: The roads are perilous and the people exhausted; public expense harms private interest.
translations.idiomatic: The roads are perilous and the people exhausted; public expense harms private welfare.

sentences.zh: 略計華州一車，官酬絹八匹三丈九尺，別有私民雇價布六十匹；

translations.literal: Roughly calculated, for one cart from Hua Province the official payment is eight bolts three zhang nine chi of silk, and private citizens must additionally hire at sixty bolts of cloth;
translations.idiomatic: By rough calculation, for one cart from Hua Province the official payment is eight bolts three zhang nine chi of silk, and private citizens must additionally pay sixty bolts of cloth for hire;

sentences.zh: 河東一車，官酬絹五匹二丈，別有私民雇價布五十匹。

translations.literal: for one cart from Hedong, the official payment is five bolts two zhang of silk, and private citizens must additionally hire at fifty bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: for one cart from Hedong the official payment is five bolts two zhang of silk, and private citizens must additionally pay fifty bolts of cloth for hire.

sentences.zh: 自餘州郡，雖未練多少，推之遠近，應不減此。

translations.literal: For the remaining provinces and commanderies, though the exact amounts are not known, extrapolating by distance they should be no less than this.
translations.idiomatic: For the remaining provinces and commanderies, though exact amounts are unknown, extrapolating by distance the costs should be no less.

sentences.zh: 今求車取雇絹三匹，市材造船，不勞採斫。

translations.literal: Now, if three bolts of silk per cart are taken for hire, timber purchased to build boats, and no labor spent on felling trees,
translations.idiomatic: If three bolts of silk per cart were taken for hire, timber purchased to build boats, and no labor spent on felling trees,

sentences.zh: 計船一艘，舉十三車，車取三匹，合有三十九匹。

translations.literal: calculated per boat, one boat equals thirteen carts; at three bolts per cart, the total comes to thirty-nine bolts.
translations.idiomatic: one boat would carry the load of thirteen carts; at three bolts per cart, the total would come to thirty-nine bolts.

sentences.zh: 雇作手并匠及船上雜具食直，足以成船。

translations.literal: Hiring laborers together with craftsmen and wages for miscellaneous shipboard provisions is sufficient to complete a boat.
translations.idiomatic: Wages for hired laborers, craftsmen, and miscellaneous shipboard supplies are enough to finish a boat.

sentences.zh: 計一船剩絹七十八匹，布七百八十匹。

translations.literal: Calculated for one boat, there remain seventy-eight bolts of silk and seven hundred eighty bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: For one boat, the surplus comes to seventy-eight bolts of silk and seven hundred eighty bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 又租車一乘，官格四十斛成載；

translations.literal: Also hiring one cart—the official standard is a full load of forty hu;
translations.idiomatic: One cart is also hired—the official standard is a full load of forty hu;

sentences.zh: 私民雇價，遠者五斗布一匹，近者一石布一匹。

translations.literal: private citizens' hire rates are one bolt of cloth per five dou for distant hauls, one bolt per one shi for near hauls.
translations.idiomatic: Private hire rates are one bolt of cloth per five dou for distant routes and one bolt per one shi for near routes.

sentences.zh: 準其私費，一車布遠者八十匹，近者四十匹。

translations.literal: Calculating by these private costs, cloth for one cart comes to eighty bolts for distant routes, forty for near routes.
translations.idiomatic: At these private rates, one cart costs eighty bolts of cloth for distant hauls and forty for near hauls.

sentences.zh: 造船一艘，計舉七百石，準其雇價，應有一千四百匹。

translations.literal: For building one boat, calculated at a capacity of seven hundred shi, at hire rates it should come to fourteen hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Building one boat with a capacity of seven hundred shi, at hire rates the cost should be fourteen hundred bolts.

sentences.zh: 今取布三百匹，造船一艘并船上覆治雜事，計一船有剩布一千一百匹。

translations.literal: Now taking three hundred bolts of cloth to build one boat including shipboard outfitting and miscellaneous matters, one boat would have a surplus of eleven hundred bolts of cloth.
