translations.literal: seven hundred shi to an outer provincial or commandery granary, or three hundred shi to the capital granary, earns the county superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred shi to an outer provincial or commandery granary, or three hundred shi to the capital granary, earns the county superintendent.

sentences.zh: 孝靜天平初，以遷民草創，資產未立，詔出粟一百三十萬石以賑之。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianping under Emperor Xiaojing, because resettled people were still establishing their livelihoods and assets had not yet been settled, an edict issued 1,300,000 shi of grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianping under Emperor Xiaojing, because resettled people were still establishing their livelihoods and had not yet acquired assets, an edict issued 1,300,000 shi of grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，又賑遷民稟各四十日。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year, resettled people were also given forty days' grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year, resettled people were also given forty days' grain rations.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，并、肆、汾、建、晉、泰、陝、東雍、南汾九州霜旱，民飢流散。

translations.literal: That autumn, frost and drought struck the nine provinces of Bing, Si, Fen, Jian, Jin, Tai, Shan, Eastern Yong, and Southern Fen; the people went hungry and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, frost and drought struck Bing, Si, Fen, Jian, Jin, Tai, Shan, Eastern Yong, and Southern Fen; the people went hungry and scattered.

sentences.zh: 四年春，詔所在開倉賑恤之，而死者甚眾。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, an edict ordered granaries opened everywhere for relief, but deaths were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, an edict ordered granaries opened everywhere for relief, but deaths were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 時諸州調絹不依舊式，齊獻武王以其害民，興和三年冬，請班海內，悉以四十尺為度。

translations.literal: At that time the provinces did not follow the old standard for tribute silk; Prince Xianwu of Qi, finding this harmful to the people, in the winter of the third year of Xinghe requested that throughout the realm the standard length be uniformly forty chi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time provinces did not follow the old standard for tribute silk; Prince Xianwu of Qi, finding this harmful to the people, in the winter of the third year of Xinghe requested that throughout the realm the standard length be uniformly forty chi.

sentences.zh: 天下利焉。

translations.literal: The realm benefited thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The realm benefited thereby.

sentences.zh: 河東郡有鹽池，舊立官司以收稅利，是時罷之，[17]而民有富強者專擅其用，貧弱者不得資益。

translations.literal: Hedong Commandery has a salt pond; formerly an official office was established to collect tax profits, but at this time it was abolished, [17] and wealthy and powerful men monopolized its use while the poor and weak could not share the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong Commandery has a salt pond; formerly an official office collected tax profits, but at this time it was abolished, [17] and wealthy and powerful men monopolized its use while the poor and weak could not share the benefit.

sentences.zh: 延興末，復立監司，量其貴賤，節其賦入，於是公私兼利。

translations.literal: At the end of Yanxing, a supervisory office was reestablished to gauge price by quality and regulate levies, and thereafter both public and private interests were served.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yanxing, a supervisory office was reestablished to gauge price by quality and regulate levies, and thereafter both public and private interests were served.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，政存寬簡，復罷其禁，與百姓共之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, his policy favored leniency and simplicity, and the prohibition was again lifted so the people might share it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, his policy favored leniency and simplicity, and the prohibition was again lifted so the people might share the salt pond jointly.

sentences.zh: 其國用所須，別為條制，取足而已。

translations.literal: What the state required was separately regulated, taking only what sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: What the state required was separately regulated, taking only what was needed.

sentences.zh: 自後豪貴之家復乘勢占奪，近池之民，又輒障吝。

translations.literal: Thereafter powerful and noble families again seized it by force; people near the pond also arbitrarily blocked access.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter powerful and noble families again seized it by force, and people near the pond also arbitrarily blocked access.

sentences.zh: 強弱相陵，聞於遠近。

translations.literal: The strong oppressed the weak, and word of it spread far and near.
translations.idiomatic: The strong oppressed the weak, and word spread far and near.

sentences.zh: 神龜初，太師、高陽王雍，太傅、清河王懌等奏：「鹽池天藏，資育羣生。

translations.literal: At the start of Shengui, Grand Tutor Prince Gaoyang Yong, Grand Preceptor Prince Qinghe Yi, and others memorialized: "The salt pond is a heaven-sent storehouse, nourishing all living things.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shengui, Grand Tutor Prince Gaoyang Yong, Grand Preceptor Prince Qinghe Yi, and others memorialized: "The salt pond is a heaven-sent storehouse, nourishing all living things.

sentences.zh: 仰惟先朝限者，亦不苟與細民競茲贏利。

translations.literal: Reflecting on how former courts limited access, they too did not lightly compete with common people for this profit.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on how former courts limited access, they too did not lightly compete with common people for this profit.

sentences.zh: 但利起天池，取用無法，或豪貴封護，或近者吝守，卑賤遠來，超然絕望。

translations.literal: But profit arose at the heavenly pool with no fixed rules; powerful families walled it off, or those nearby guarded it jealously, so the humble and distant came and despaired utterly.
translations.idiomatic: But profit arose at the heavenly pool with no fixed rules; powerful families walled it off, or those nearby guarded it jealously, so the humble and distant came and despaired utterly.

sentences.zh: 是以因置主司，令其裁察，強弱相兼，務令得所。

translations.literal: Therefore a chief office was established to oversee and judge, so strong and weak might share alike and each receive what was due.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore a chief office was established to oversee and judge, so strong and weak might share alike and each receive what was due.

sentences.zh: 且十一之稅，自古及今，取輒以次，所濟為廣。

translations.literal: Moreover the one-tenth tax, from antiquity to the present, has been collected in order, and the benefit it provides is broad.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the one-tenth tax, from antiquity to the present, has been collected in order, and the benefit it provides is broad.

sentences.zh: 自爾霑洽，遠近齊平，公私兩宜，儲益不少。

translations.literal: From then on benefits spread everywhere; near and far were alike balanced; public and private interests were both served; and stores increased considerably.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the benefits spread everywhere; near and far were brought into balance, public and private interests were both served, and state reserves grew substantially.

sentences.zh: 及鼓吹主簿王後興等詞稱請供百官食鹽二萬斛之外，歲求輸馬千匹、牛五百頭。

translations.literal: Moreover the director of the imperial music bureau Wang Houxing and others petitioned, claiming that beyond supplying twenty thousand hu of salt for officials' food, they requested each year to deliver one thousand horses and five hundred head of cattle.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Wang Houxing, director of the imperial music bureau, and others petitioned that, beyond supplying twenty thousand hu of salt for officials' rations, they should each year deliver one thousand horses and five hundred head of cattle.

sentences.zh: 以此而推，非可稍計。

translations.literal: Extrapolating from this, it cannot be reckoned as a small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating from this, the burden cannot be dismissed as trivial.

sentences.zh: 後中尉甄琛啟求罷禁，被敕付議。

translations.literal: Later Commandant of Justice Zhen Chen memorialized requesting the abolition of the prohibition, and received an edict referring the matter for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Later Commandant of Justice Zhen Chen memorialized asking that the prohibition be lifted, and an edict referred the matter for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 尚書執奏，稱琛啟坐談則理高，行之則事闕，請依常禁為允。

translations.literal: The Ministry of State Affairs submitted a firm memorial, stating that Zhen Chen's proposal was lofty in discussion but deficient in practice, and requesting that the usual prohibition be maintained as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of State Affairs submitted a firm memorial arguing that Zhen Chen's proposal sounded fine in theory but would fail in practice, and asking that the usual prohibition be kept in place.

sentences.zh: 詔依琛計。

translations.literal: An edict followed Zhen Chen's plan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved Zhen Chen's plan.

sentences.zh: 乃為繞池之民尉保光等擅自固護，語其障禁，倍於官司，取與自由，貴賤任口。

translations.literal: Thereupon the people around the pond such as Wei Baoguang on their own authority fortified and guarded it; speaking of their barriers and prohibitions, they were double those of the official offices; they took and gave as they pleased and fixed prices at will for noble and base alike.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon people around the pond such as Wei Baoguang took it upon themselves to fortify and guard the site; their barriers and restrictions were twice as strict as the government's; they traded as they pleased and set prices at will for rich and poor alike.

sentences.zh: 若無大宥，罪合推斷。

translations.literal: If not granted a general amnesty, the crime warrants prosecution and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Without a general amnesty, these offenses warrant prosecution and punishment.

sentences.zh: 詳度二三，深乖王法。

translations.literal: Considering the matter two or three times over, this deeply violates the royal law.
translations.idiomatic: On careful reconsideration, this flagrantly violates the law of the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣等商量，請依先朝之詔，禁之為便。

translations.literal: We your ministers have deliberated and request that it be prohibited according to the former dynasty's edict, which would be expedient.
translations.idiomatic: We your ministers have deliberated and ask that the prohibition be restored according to the former dynasty's edict, which would be the prudent course.

sentences.zh: 防姦息暴，斷遣輕重，亦準前旨。

translations.literal: Preventing wickedness and quelling violence, and determining severity in sentencing, should also follow the prior intent.
translations.idiomatic: Preventing abuse, suppressing violence, and determining sentences according to severity should likewise follow the earlier policy.

sentences.zh: 所置監司，一同往式。

translations.literal: The supervisory offices established should all follow the former pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisory offices to be established should all follow the former model.

sentences.zh: 」於是復置監官以監檢焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon supervisory officials were again established to inspect and oversee.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon supervisory officials were again appointed to inspect and oversee the pond.

sentences.zh: 其後更罷更立，以至於永熙。

translations.literal: Afterward they were repeatedly abolished and reestablished, continuing until the Yongxi era.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the offices were repeatedly abolished and reestablished, a cycle that continued until the Yongxi era.

sentences.zh: 自遷鄴後，於滄、瀛、幽、青四州之境，傍海煑鹽。

translations.literal: After the capital was moved to Ye, salt was boiled along the coast within the territories of the four prefectures Cang, Ying, You, and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was moved to Ye, salt was boiled along the coast in the territories of the four prefectures of Cang, Ying, You, and Qing.

sentences.zh: 滄州置竈一千四百八十四，瀛州置竈四百五十二，幽州置竈一百八十，青州置竈五百四十六，又於邯鄲置竈四，計終歲合收鹽二十萬九千七百二斛四升。

translations.literal: Cang Prefecture had 1,484 furnaces installed, Ying Prefecture 452, You Prefecture 180, and Qing Prefecture 546; four more furnaces were placed at Handan; in total the year's collection amounted to 209,702 hu and 4 sheng of salt.
translations.idiomatic: Cang Prefecture had 1,484 furnaces, Ying 452, You 180, and Qing 546; four more were placed at Handan; in all, the year's salt yield came to 209,702 hu and 4 sheng.

sentences.zh: 軍國所資，得以周贍矣。

translations.literal: What the army and state required could thus be fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: The needs of army and state could thus be fully met.

sentences.zh: 魏初至於太和，錢貨無所周流，高祖始詔天下用錢焉。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Wei until the Taihe era, money and goods did not circulate; Emperor Gaozu first decreed that the realm should use coin.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of Wei until the Taihe era, money scarcely circulated at all; Emperor Gaozu was the first to decree that coin should be used throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 十九年，冶鑄粗備，文曰「太和五銖」，詔京師及諸州鎮皆通行之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, smelting and casting were largely ready; the inscription read "Taihe Five Zhu"; an edict ordered circulation throughout the capital and all prefectures and garrison towns.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year smelting and casting were largely in place; the coins were inscribed "Taihe Five Zhu," and an edict ordered them circulated throughout the capital and all prefectures and garrison towns.

sentences.zh: 內外百官祿皆準絹給錢，絹匹為錢二百。

translations.literal: Salaries for all officials within and without the court were converted from silk to coin at the rate of two hundred coins per bolt of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Salaries for all officials inside and outside the court were converted from silk to coin at two hundred coins per bolt.

sentences.zh: 在所遣錢工備爐冶，民有欲鑄，聽就鑄之，銅必精練，無所和雜。

translations.literal: Wherever coin workers were dispatched, furnaces were prepared; if people wished to cast coin, they were permitted to cast there, but the copper had to be finely refined with no admixture.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever coin workers were dispatched, furnaces were set up; those who wished to cast coin were permitted to do so on site, provided the copper was finely refined and nothing was mixed in.

sentences.zh: 世宗永平三年冬，又鑄五銖錢。

translations.literal: In winter of the third year of Yongping under Emperor Shizong, Five Zhu coins were cast again.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Yongping under Emperor Shizong, Five Zhu coins were cast again.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，京師及諸州鎮或鑄或否，或有止用古錢，不行新鑄，致商貨不通，貿遷頗隔。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign, in the capital and garrison towns some cast coins and some did not; some used only old coins and would not accept newly cast ones, causing commerce to stall and trade to be heavily obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Suzong's reign, some prefectures and garrison towns cast coin and some did not; some accepted only old coin and rejected new issues, so commerce stalled and trade was badly disrupted.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，尚書令、任城王澄上言：「臣聞洪範八政，貨居二焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping, Minister of State Affairs, Prince of Rencheng, Cheng submitted: "Your subject has heard that among the eight administrative concerns in the Hong Fan, goods and currency rank second.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiping, Minister of State Affairs Prince of Rencheng Cheng submitted: "Your subject has heard that among the eight administrative concerns in the Hong Fan, goods and currency rank second.

sentences.zh: 易稱：『天地之大德曰生，聖人之大寶曰位，何以守位曰仁，何以聚人曰財。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called giving life; the great treasure of the sage is called position; by what does one hold position? By benevolence. By what does one gather people? By wealth.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: 'The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is to give life; the great treasure of the sage is his throne; by what does he hold his throne? By benevolence. By what does he gather the people? By wealth.'

sentences.zh: 』財者，帝王所以聚人守位，成養羣生，奉順天德，治國安民之本也。

translations.literal: ' Wealth is what emperors and kings use to gather people and hold their position, to nurture all living beings, to obey Heaven's virtue—the foundation of governing the state and settling the people.
translations.idiomatic: ' Wealth is what emperors and kings use to gather the people and hold their thrones, to nurture all living beings and obey Heaven's virtue—it is the foundation of governing the state and securing the people.

sentences.zh: 夏殷之政，九州貢金，以定五品。

translations.literal: Under the governments of Xia and Yin, the nine provinces presented tribute in gold, by which the five ranks were established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xia and Yin, the nine provinces paid tribute in gold, and by this the five ranks were established.

sentences.zh: 周仍其舊。

translations.literal: Zhou continued the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou continued the old practice.

sentences.zh: 太公立九府之法，於是圜貨始行，[18]定銖兩之楷。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou established the law of the nine treasuries, and then round currency first circulated, [18] fixing the standard of zhu and liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou established the law of the nine treasuries, and round currency first came into use, [18] fixing the standard of zhu and liang.

sentences.zh: 齊桓循用，以霸諸侯。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi followed and employed it, thereby dominating the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi adopted it and thereby dominated the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 降及秦始、漢文，遂有輕重之異。

translations.literal: Descending to Qin Shihuang and Emperor Wen of Han, there then arose differences in weight.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wen of Han, differences in weight had appeared.

sentences.zh: 吳濞、鄧通之錢，收利遍於天下，河南之地，猶甚多焉。

translations.literal: The coins of Liu Pi and Deng Tong, their profits spread throughout the realm; in the region south of the Yellow River there were still very many of them.
translations.idiomatic: The coin of Liu Pi and Deng Tong spread their profits across the realm, and south of the Yellow River there were still very many in circulation.

sentences.zh: 逮于孝武，乃更造五銖，其中毀鑄，隨利改易，故使錢有小大之品。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Xiaowu of Han, they remade the Five Zhu; amid destruction and recasting, altered at will for profit, hence coins came in large and small types.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Han the Five Zhu was remade, but coins were melted down and recast for profit as circumstances dictated, so money came in large and small denominations.

sentences.zh: 竊尋太和之錢，高祖留心創制，後與五銖並行，此乃不刊之式。

translations.literal: Privately examining the Taihe coins—Emperor Gaozu attentively created them; afterward they circulated alongside the Five Zhu. This is an immutable standard.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on the Taihe coin, Emperor Gaozu took care to create it anew; afterward it circulated alongside the Five Zhu. This is an immutable standard.

sentences.zh: 但臣竊聞之，君子行禮，不求變俗，因其所宜，順而致用。

translations.literal: But your subject has privately heard that when the superior man practices ritual, he does not seek to alter local customs; he adapts to what is suitable and applies things accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: But your subject has heard it said that when the superior man practices ritual, he does not seek to change local custom; he adapts to what is suitable and puts things to use accordingly.

sentences.zh: 『太和五銖』雖利於京邑之肆，而不入徐揚之市。

translations.literal: Although the "Taihe Five Zhu" benefits shops in the capital, it does not enter markets in Xu and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Although the "Taihe Five Zhu" serves the shops of the capital well, it does not circulate in the markets of Xu and Yang.

sentences.zh: 土貨既殊，貿鬻亦異，便於荊郢之邦者，則礙於兗豫之域。

translations.literal: Local products differ, and trade differs as well; what suits the lands of Jing and Ying hampers the region of Yan and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Local products differ, and trade differs with them; what works in the lands of Jing and Ying proves awkward in the region of Yan and Yu.

sentences.zh: 致使貧民有重困之切，王道貽隔化之訟。

translations.literal: This causes the poor acute distress, and kingly governance to suffer disputes born of alienation from transformation.
translations.idiomatic: This leaves the poor in acute distress and brings disputes that alienate the people from the kingly way.

sentences.zh: 去永平三年，都座奏斷天下用錢不依準式者，時被敕云：『不行之錢，雖有常禁，其先用之處，權可聽行，至年末悉令斷之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongping, the chief seat memorialized to cut off throughout the realm the use of coin not conforming to the standard; at the time they received an edict saying: 'Non-standard coin, though regularly prohibited, may for the time being be permitted where it is already in use, but by year's end all use is to be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongping the chief seat memorialized to ban throughout the realm coin that did not conform to the standard; the response was an edict saying: 'Non-standard coin, though regularly prohibited, may for the time being be tolerated where it is already in use, but by year's end all such use is to cease.

sentences.zh: 』延昌二年，徐州民儉，刺史啟奏求行土錢，旨聽權依舊用。

translations.literal: ' In the second year of Yanzhang, the people of Xu Province were impoverished; the governor memorialized requesting permission to use local coin, and the imperial directive permitted temporary continued use of the old coin.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the second year of Yanzhang the people of Xu Province were impoverished; the governor memorialized asking to use local coin, and the throne permitted temporary continued use of the old currency.

sentences.zh: 謹尋不行之錢，律有明式，指謂雞眼、[19]鐶鑿，更無餘禁。

translations.literal: Carefully examining non-standard coin, the law has a clear formula, referring specifically to chicken-eye, [19] ring-chisel coins, with no further prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: On careful review, the law defines non-standard coin clearly: it refers specifically to chicken-eye, [19] ring-chisel coins, and nothing else is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 計河南諸州，今所行者，悉非制限。

translations.literal: Considering the provinces south of the Yellow River, what is now in circulation is entirely outside the prescribed limits.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the provinces south of the Yellow River, what is now in circulation falls entirely outside the prescribed limits.

sentences.zh: 昔來繩禁，愚竊惑焉。

translations.literal: The prohibitions enforced until now—your subject is privately perplexed by them.
translations.idiomatic: The prohibitions enforced until now leave your subject privately perplexed.

sentences.zh: 又河北州鎮，既無新造五銖，設有舊者，而復禁斷，並不得行，專以單絲之縑，疏縷之布，狹幅促度，不中常式，裂匹為尺，以濟有無。

translations.literal: Moreover in the garrison towns north of the Yellow River, since there is no newly cast Five Zhu, even where old coin exists it is again prohibited and may not circulate; they rely solely on single-thread silk, loosely woven cloth, narrow width and short measure—not conforming to the usual standard—tearing bolts into foot-lengths to meet needs.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover in the garrison towns north of the Yellow River, where no new Five Zhu has been cast, even old coin is banned and may not circulate; people rely solely on single-thread silk and loosely woven cloth of narrow width and short measure—not conforming to the usual standard—tearing bolts into foot-lengths to meet their needs.

sentences.zh: 至今徒成杼軸之勞，[20]不免飢寒之苦，良由分截布帛，壅塞錢貨。

translations.literal: To this day they merely incur the labor of loom and spindle, [20] yet cannot escape hunger and cold—the real cause being the cutting up of cloth and silk and the blocking of money and goods.
translations.idiomatic: To this day they merely incur the labor of loom and spindle, [20] yet cannot escape hunger and cold—the real cause being the cutting up of cloth and silk and the blocking of coin.

sentences.zh: 實非救恤凍餒，子育黎元。

translations.literal: This truly is not relieving the cold and hungry or nurturing the common people.
translations.idiomatic: This is hardly the way to relieve the cold and hungry or nurture the common people.

sentences.zh: 謹惟自古以來，錢品不一，前後累代，易變無常。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering from antiquity to the present, coin types have not been uniform; dynasty after dynasty they have changed without fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting from antiquity to the present, coin types have never been uniform; dynasty after dynasty they have changed without fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 且錢之為名，欲泉流不已。

translations.literal: Moreover the very name of coin signifies the wish that it flow like a spring without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the very name of coin signifies the wish that it flow like a spring without end.

sentences.zh: 愚意謂今之太和與新鑄五銖，及諸古錢方俗所便用者，雖有大小之異，並得通行。

translations.literal: Your subject's humble opinion is that the present Taihe and newly cast Five Zhu, together with all old coins convenient to local custom, though differing in size, should all be permitted to circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's humble opinion is that the present Taihe and newly cast Five Zhu, together with all old coins that local custom finds convenient, though they differ in size, should all be permitted to circulate.

sentences.zh: 貴賤之差，自依鄉價。

translations.literal: Differences in value should follow local prices.
translations.idiomatic: Differences in value should follow local market prices.

sentences.zh: 庶貨環海內，公私無壅。

translations.literal: Thus goods may circulate throughout the realm, and public and private interests suffer no obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Thus goods may circulate throughout the realm, and neither public nor private interest will be blocked.

sentences.zh: 其不行之錢，及盜鑄毀大為小，巧偽不如法者，據律罪之。

translations.literal: As for non-standard coin, and illicit casting or melting large coins into small ones, or clever counterfeits not conforming to law—these should be punished according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: Non-standard coin, illicit casting, melting large coins into small ones, and clever counterfeits that fail to meet the law should all be punished according to statute.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「錢行已久，今東尚有事，[21]且依舊用。」

translations.literal: " The edict said: "Coin has circulated for a long time; the east still has affairs underway, [21] so for now continue using the old coin."
translations.idiomatic: " The edict replied: "Coin has circulated for a long time; affairs in the east are still unsettled, [21] so for now continue using the old currency."

sentences.zh: 澄又奏：「臣猥屬樞衡，庶罄心力，常願貨物均通，書軌一範。

translations.literal: Cheng again memorialized: "Your subject, unworthy though entrusted with the pivot of government, hopes to exhaust his strength, ever wishing that goods circulate evenly and writing and ruts share one standard.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized again: "Your subject, unworthy though he is of his post at the pivot of government, hopes to give his full strength to the wish that goods circulate freely and that writing and wheel ruts share one standard throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 謹詳周禮，外府掌邦布之入出。

translations.literal: Carefully examining the Rites of Zhou, the outer treasury manages the receipt and disbursement of the state's currency.
translations.idiomatic: On careful review of the Rites of Zhou, the outer treasury manages the receipt and disbursement of the state's currency.

sentences.zh: 布猶泉也，其藏曰泉，其流曰布。

translations.literal: Currency is like a spring: what is stored is called a spring; what flows is called currency.
translations.idiomatic: Currency is like a spring: what is stored is called a spring, and what flows is called currency.

sentences.zh: 然則錢之興也始於一品，欲令世匠均同，圜流無極。

translations.literal: Thus the rise of coin began with a single type, intending that craftsmen throughout the age make them uniformly alike, circulating round without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Thus coin arose as a single standard, so that craftsmen throughout the age would make it uniformly and it would circulate without limit.

sentences.zh: 爰暨周景，降逮亡新，易鑄相尋，參差百品，遂令接境乖商，連邦隔貿。

translations.literal: From the time of King Jing of Zhou down to the Xin dynasty, recastings followed one after another in a hundred irregular types, until neighboring borders fell out of commerce and adjoining states were cut off from trade.
translations.idiomatic: From the time of King Jing of Zhou down to the Xin dynasty, recastings followed one after another in a hundred irregular types, until neighboring borders fell out of commerce and adjoining states were cut off from trade.

sentences.zh: [22]臣比奏求宣下海內，依式行錢。

translations.literal: [22] Your subject recently memorialized requesting that it be proclaimed throughout the realm and coin circulated according to the standard.
translations.idiomatic: [22] Your subject recently memorialized asking that coin be proclaimed throughout the realm and circulated according to the standard.

sentences.zh: 登被旨敕，『錢行已久，且可依舊』。

translations.literal: Upon receiving the imperial directive: 'Coin has circulated for a long time; for now continue according to the old practice.'
translations.idiomatic: The response was an imperial directive: 'Coin has circulated for a long time; for now continue according to the old practice.'

sentences.zh: 謹重參量，以為『太和五銖』乃大魏之通貨，不朽之恒模，寧可專貿於京邑，不行於天下！

translations.literal: Respectfully reconsidering, your subject holds that the "Taihe Five Zhu" is Great Wei's general currency, an immutable constant model—how can it be traded only in the capital and not circulate throughout the realm!
translations.idiomatic: On reconsideration, your subject holds that the "Taihe Five Zhu" is Great Wei's general currency, an immutable constant model—how can it circulate only in the capital and not throughout the realm!

sentences.zh: 但今戎馬在郊，江疆未一，東南之州，依舊為便。

translations.literal: But now war-horses are at the suburbs; the Yangtze frontier is not yet unified; in the southeastern provinces, the old practice remains convenient.
translations.idiomatic: But war-horses are at the gates, the Yangtze frontier is not yet unified, and in the southeastern provinces the old practice remains the practical choice.

sentences.zh: 至於京西、京北域內州鎮未用錢處，行之則不足為難，塞之則有乖通典。

translations.literal: As for the prefectures and garrison towns within the realm west and north of the capital where coin is not yet used, to introduce it would not be difficult, but to block it would violate the universal norm.
translations.idiomatic: As for the prefectures and garrison towns west and north of the capital where coin is not yet used, introducing it would not be difficult, but blocking it would violate the universal norm.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 布帛不可尺寸而裂，五穀則有負檐之難，錢之為用，貫繈相屬，不假斗斛之器，不勞秤尺之平，濟世之宜，謂為深允。

translations.literal: Cloth and silk cannot be torn by the inch; the five grains pose the difficulty of carrying on the shoulder; as for the use of coin, strings of cash link one to another—it needs no bushel or peck measure, requires no labor of scales and rulers—and for serving the age, this is deemed deeply fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Cloth and silk cannot conveniently be torn by the inch; grain is hard to carry on the shoulder; but coin passes from hand to hand in linked strings—it needs no bushel measure, no labor of scales and rulers—and for serving the age, nothing could be more apt.

sentences.zh: 請並下諸方州鎮，其太和及新鑄五銖并古錢內外全好者，不限大小，悉聽行之。

translations.literal: Your subject requests that orders be sent to all prefectures and garrison towns: Taihe and newly cast Five Zhu together with old coins that are intact inside and out, regardless of size, should all be permitted to circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject asks that orders be sent to all prefectures and garrison towns permitting Taihe and newly cast Five Zhu, together with old coin that is intact inside and out, regardless of size, to circulate freely.

sentences.zh: 雞眼、鐶鑿，依律而禁。

translations.literal: Chicken-eye and ring-chisel coins should be prohibited according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Chicken-eye and ring-chisel coins should be banned according to law.

sentences.zh: 河南州鎮先用錢者，既聽依舊，不在斷限。

translations.literal: The prefectures and garrison towns south of the Yellow River that already use coin are permitted to continue as before and are not within the cutoff limit.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and garrison towns south of the Yellow River that already use coin are permitted to continue as before and are not subject to the cutoff.

sentences.zh: 唯太和、五銖二錢得用公造新者，其餘雜種，一用古錢，生新之類，普同禁約。

translations.literal: Only for Taihe and Five Zhu coin may newly minted official coin be used; all other miscellaneous types, whether old coin alone or newly made private coin, should be universally prohibited alike.
translations.idiomatic: Only Taihe and Five Zhu may be newly minted by the state; all other miscellaneous types, whether old coin alone or privately made new coin, should be universally prohibited.

sentences.zh: 諸方之錢，通用京師，其聽依舊之處，與太和錢及新造五銖並行，若盜鑄者罪重常憲。

translations.literal: Coin from all regions should circulate in the capital; where old practice is permitted, it should circulate alongside Taihe coin and newly cast Five Zhu; illicit casters should be punished more heavily than ordinary law provides.
translations.idiomatic: Coin from all regions should circulate in the capital; where old practice is permitted, it should circulate alongside Taihe coin and newly cast Five Zhu; illicit casters should be punished more heavily than ordinary law provides.

sentences.zh: 既欲均齊物品，廛井斯和，若不繩以嚴法，無以肅茲違犯。

translations.literal: Since the wish is to equalize goods and harmonize markets, if not bound by strict law, there is no means to discipline these violations.
translations.idiomatic: Since the aim is to equalize goods and harmonize markets, without strict law there is no way to discipline these violations.

sentences.zh: 符旨一宣，仍不遵用者，刺史守令依律治罪。

translations.literal: Once the directive is proclaimed, those who still do not comply—governors, prefects, and magistrates—should be punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Once the directive is proclaimed, governors, prefects, and magistrates who still fail to comply should be punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 而河北諸州，舊少錢貨，猶以他物交易，錢略不入市也。

translations.literal: But in the provinces north of the Yellow River, coin had long been scarce; they still traded in other goods, and coin scarcely entered the markets at all.
translations.idiomatic: But in the provinces north of the Yellow River coin had long been scarce; people still traded in other goods, and coin scarcely entered the markets at all.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，尚書崔亮奏：「恒農郡銅青谷有銅鑛，計一斗得銅五兩四銖；

translations.literal: In the second year, winter, Minister Cui Liang memorialized: "In Tongqing Valley, Hengnong Commandery, there is a copper mine; calculating from one dou yields five liang and four zhu of copper;
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year, Minister Cui Liang memorialized: "Tongqing Valley in Hengnong Commandery has a copper mine; one dou of ore yields five liang and four zhu of copper;

sentences.zh: 葦池谷鑛，計一斗得銅五兩；

translations.literal: Weichi Valley mine: calculating from one dou yields five liang of copper;
translations.idiomatic: Weichi Valley mine: one dou of ore yields five liang of copper;

sentences.zh: 鸞帳山鑛，計一斗得銅四兩；

translations.literal: Luanzhang Mountain mine: calculating from one dou yields four liang of copper;
translations.idiomatic: Luanzhang Mountain mine: one dou of ore yields four liang of copper;

sentences.zh: 河內郡王屋山鑛，計一斗得銅八兩；

translations.literal: Wangwu Mountain mine, Henei Commandery: calculating from one dou yields eight liang of copper;
translations.idiomatic: Wangwu Mountain mine in Henei Commandery: one dou of ore yields eight liang of copper;

sentences.zh: 南青州苑燭山、齊州商山並是往昔銅官，舊迹見在。

translations.literal: Yuanzhu Mountain in Southern Qing Province and Shang Mountain in Qi Province were both former copper offices of old; their traces still remain.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhu Mountain in Southern Qing Province and Shang Mountain in Qi Province were both former state copper offices; their traces still remain.

sentences.zh: 謹按鑄錢方興，用銅處廣，既有冶利，並宜開鑄。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering that coin casting is just beginning and copper is needed widely, since smelting yields profit, all should be opened for casting.
translations.idiomatic: Since coin casting is just beginning and copper is needed widely, and smelting yields profit, all these sites should be opened for casting.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 自後所行之錢，民多私鑄，稍就小薄，價用彌賤。

translations.literal: Afterward the coin in circulation was largely privately cast by the people, gradually growing smaller and thinner, and its purchasing power ever cheaper.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward much of the coin in circulation was privately cast; it gradually grew smaller and thinner, and its value ever cheaper.

sentences.zh: 建義初，重盜鑄之禁，開糾賞之格。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, the prohibition on illicit casting was strengthened and a reward scale for informants was established.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianyi the prohibition on illicit casting was strengthened and rewards for informants were established.

sentences.zh: 至永安二年秋，詔更改鑄，文曰「永安五銖」，官自立爐，起自九月至三年正月而止。

translations.literal: By autumn of the second year of Yong'an, an edict ordered recoining; the inscription read "Yong'an Five Zhu"; the government set up its own furnaces, operating from the ninth month until the first month of the third year.
translations.idiomatic: By the autumn of the second year of Yong'an an edict ordered recoining; the inscription read "Yong'an Five Zhu"; the government set up its own furnaces, operating from the ninth month until the first month of the third year.

sentences.zh: 官欲貴錢，乃出藏絹，分遣使人於二市賣之，[23]絹匹止錢二百，而私市者猶三百。

translations.literal: The government wishing to raise the value of coin, released silk from the treasury and dispatched envoys to sell it in the two markets, [23] at two hundred coins per bolt of silk, while in private markets it still fetched three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to raise the value of coin, the government released silk from the treasury and dispatched envoys to sell it in the two markets, [23] at two hundred coins per bolt, while in private markets it still fetched three hundred.

sentences.zh: 利之所在，盜鑄彌眾，巧偽既多，輕重非一，四方州鎮，用各不同。

translations.literal: Where profit lay, illicit casting multiplied; clever counterfeits grew numerous; weights were not uniform; and prefectures and garrison towns in all directions used coin differently.
translations.idiomatic: Where profit lay, illicit casting multiplied; counterfeits grew numerous; weights varied; and prefectures and garrison towns everywhere used coin differently.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴之後，輕濫尤多。

translations.literal: After the move to Ye, debased coin was especially abundant.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Ye, debased coin was especially abundant.

sentences.zh: 武定初，齊文襄王奏革其弊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding, Prince Wenxiang of Qi memorialized to reform these abuses.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wuding, Prince Wenxiang of Qi memorialized to reform these abuses.

sentences.zh: 於是詔遣使人詣諸州鎮，收銅及錢，悉更改鑄，其文仍舊。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict dispatched envoys to all prefectures and garrison towns to collect copper and coin, recoining all of it; the inscription remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict dispatched envoys to all prefectures and garrison towns to collect copper and coin and recoin all of it; the inscription remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 然姦僥之徒，越法趨利，未幾之間，漸復細薄。

translations.literal: Yet scheming opportunists, transgressing law to pursue profit, in no long time gradually made the coin thin and small again.
translations.idiomatic: Yet scheming opportunists, breaking the law for profit, soon made the coin thin and small again.

sentences.zh: 六年，文襄王以錢文五銖，名須稱實，宜稱錢一文重五銖者，聽入市用。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Prince Wenxiang held that since the coin's inscription was Five Zhu, the name must match the reality: only coin of one wen weighing five zhu should be permitted for market use.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Prince Wenxiang held that since the coin was inscribed Five Zhu, the name must match the reality: only coin weighing five zhu per wen should be permitted in the markets.

sentences.zh: 計百錢重一斤四兩二十銖，自餘皆準此為數。

translations.literal: Calculating one hundred coins at one jin, four liang, and twenty zhu; all others should follow this as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred coins should weigh one jin, four liang, and twenty zhu; all other denominations should follow this standard.

sentences.zh: 其京邑二市、天下州鎮郡縣之市，各置二稱，懸於市門，私民所用之稱，皆準市稱以定輕重。

translations.literal: In the two markets of the capital and in markets of prefectures, garrison towns, commanderies, and counties throughout the realm, two sets of scales were to be placed, hung at the market gates; the scales used privately by the people should all be calibrated against the market scales to determine weight.
translations.idiomatic: In the two markets of the capital and in markets of every prefecture, garrison town, commandery, and county, two official sets of scales were to be hung at the market gates; private scales used by the people were all to be calibrated against the market scales.

sentences.zh: 凡有私鑄，悉不禁斷，但重五銖，然後聽用。

translations.literal: All private casting was not prohibited, provided the coin weighed five zhu, after which it might be used.
translations.idiomatic: Private casting was not prohibited outright, provided each coin weighed five zhu; only then might it be used.

sentences.zh: 若入市之錢，重不五銖，或雖重五銖而多雜鉛鑞，並不聽用。

translations.literal: If coin entering the market weighed less than five zhu, or though weighing five zhu contained much lead and tin alloy, none of it was permitted for use.
translations.idiomatic: Coin entering the market that weighed less than five zhu, or that weighed five zhu but contained much lead and tin alloy, was not permitted for use.

sentences.zh: 若有輒以小薄雜錢入市，有人糾獲，其錢悉入告者。

translations.literal: If anyone brought thin, small, debased coin into the market and someone reported and seized it, all the coin went to the informant.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone brought thin, debased coin into the market and was reported and seized, all the coin went to the informant.

sentences.zh: 其小薄之錢，若即禁斷，恐人交乏絕。

translations.literal: As for the thin, small coin, if it were immediately prohibited, the fear is that people's exchanges would be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: If thin, small coin were banned immediately, trade might come to a halt.

sentences.zh: 畿內五十日，外州百日為限。

translations.literal: Within the capital region the limit was fifty days; in outer provinces, one hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Within the capital region the limit was fifty days; in outer provinces, one hundred days.

sentences.zh: 羣官參議，咸以時穀頗貴，請待有年。

translations.literal: Officials deliberated jointly, all holding that grain was then quite expensive, and requesting to wait for a good harvest year.
translations.idiomatic: Officials deliberated jointly; all held that grain was then quite expensive and asked to wait for a good harvest year.

sentences.zh: 上從之而止。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and the measure was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and the measure was dropped.

translations.literal: "Fine cocoon silk" is written as "chou cocoon silk."
translations.idiomatic: It reads "chou cocoon silk" for "fine cocoon silk."

sentences.zh: 按北史卷九０仇洛齊傳作「紬綾」，疑「細」乃「紬」形近而訛，但本書卷九四仇洛齊傳也作「細繭」，今不改。

translations.literal: Comment: Beishi juan 90, Biography of Qiu Luoqi, writes "chou gauze"; suspect "fine" is an error for the graphically similar "chou", but this book's juan 94 Biography of Qiu Luoqi also writes "fine cocoon silk" — no change made.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Beishi juan 90's biography of Qiu Luoqi has "chou gauze"; "fine" may be a near-form error for "chou", yet Wei Shu juan 94's Qiu Luoqi biography also reads "fine cocoon silk" — left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 其司冀雍華定相泰 諸本「泰」作「秦」。

translations.literal: These: Si, Ji, Yong, Hua, Ding, Xiang, Tai — in all editions "Tai" is written as "Qin."
translations.idiomatic: On "Si, Ji, Yong, Hua, Ding, Xiang, and Tai": all editions write "Tai" as "Qin."

sentences.zh: 按下出麻布諸州中又見「秦州」，而此為出綿絹及絲之十九州之一，知非一州。

translations.literal: Comment: Below, among the provinces that produce hemp cloth, "Qin Province" also appears; yet this is one of the nineteen provinces that produce floss-silk, silk, and thread — thus it cannot be a single province.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "Qin Province" appears again among hemp-cloth provinces below, but this line lists one of nineteen silk-producing provinces — so it cannot mean a single province name.

sentences.zh: 下文又舉「以麻布充稅」的郡縣有「秦州河東之蒲坂、汾陰」，與司、懷等州既在出綿絹州之中，而又舉出所屬個別郡縣「以麻布充稅」同例。

translations.literal: Below, the commanderies and counties that "pay tax in hemp cloth" include "Pupu and Fenyin in Hedong of Qin Province"; the same pattern applies to Si and Huai provinces — already within the silk-producing provinces, yet individual subordinate commanderies and counties are likewise listed as "paying tax in hemp cloth."
translations.idiomatic: Later the text names Pupu and Fenyin in Hedong of Qin Province among counties paying tax in hemp cloth — the same pattern as Si and Huai, which are silk provinces yet include individual counties taxed in hemp.

sentences.zh: 卷一０六下地形志下治蒲坂之「秦州」實為「泰州」之訛，已改正，

translations.idiomatic: In Geography B juan 106, the "Qin Province" governing Pupu was actually "Tai Province" — already corrected there,

translations.idiomatic: This "Qin" and the "Qin" in "Hedong of Qin Province" below are likewise Tai miswritten — both emended here.

sentences.zh: 皇興四年置邵上郡，太和中併河內，孝昌中改邵郡。

translations.idiomatic: Shaoshang Commandery was founded in Huangxing 4, merged into Henei under Taihe, and renamed Shao Commandery in Xiaochang.
